1.heading: Title and extent of operation of the Code.
1.canonical_text: This Act is named the Indian Penal Code and extends to the whole of India.

2.heading: Punishment of offences committed within India.
2.canonical_text: Every person is liable to punishment under this Code for acts or omissions committed within India that are contrary to its provisions, and not otherwise.

3.heading: Punishment of offences committed beyond, but which by law may be tried within, India.
3.canonical_text: This section specifies that a person liable under Indian law for an offence committed outside India shall be dealt with according to this Code as if the act occurred within India.

ingredients.text: Any person is liable, by any Indian law, to be tried for an offence.
Such a person shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Code.
The act committed beyond India is treated in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India.

4.heading: Extension of Code to extra-territorial offences.
4.canonical_text: The provisions of this Code apply to offences committed by Indian citizens outside India, by any person on Indian-registered ships or aircraft wherever they may be, and by any person outside India targeting a computer resource located in India.

ingredients.text: The provisions of this Code apply also to any offence committed by any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India.

5.heading: Certain laws not to be affected by this Act.
5.canonical_text: This Act does not affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India, nor does it affect the provisions of any special or local law.

ingredients.text: Every definition of an offence, penal provision, and illustration in this Code shall be understood subject to the exceptions contained in the Chapter entitled “General Exceptions”.

20.heading: “Court of Justice”.
20.canonical_text: The section defines 'Court of Justice' as a Judge or body of Judges empowered by law to act judicially, when acting judicially, and provides an example of a Panchayat.

21.heading: “Public servant”.
21.canonical_text: This section defines the term 'public servant' by listing various categories of individuals who fall under this designation, including military officers, judges, court officers, jurors, arbitrators, government officers, and those involved in elections or public service for government or local authorities, along with clarifying explanations regarding appointment and actual possession of office.

ingredients.text: Every Commissioned Officer in the Military, Naval or Air Forces of India.
Every Judge including any person empowered by law to discharge, whether by himself or as a member of any body of persons, any adjudicatory functions.

Every officer of a Court of Justice (including a liquidator, receiver or commissioner) whose duty it is, as such officer, to investigate or report on any matter of law or fact, or to make, authenticate, or keep any document, or to take charge or dispose of any property, or to execute any judicial process, or to administer any oath, or to interpret, or to preserve order in the Court, and every person specially authorised by a Court of Justice to perform any of such duties.
Every juryman, assessor, or member of a panchayat assisting a Court of Justice or public servant.
Every arbitrator or other person to whom any cause or matter has been referred for decision or report by any Court of Justice, or by any other competent public authority.
Every person who holds any office by virtue of which he is empowered to place or keep any person in confinement.

Every officer of the Government whose duty it is, as such officer, to prevent offences, to give information of offences, to bring offenders to justice, or to protect the public health, safety or convenience.

Every officer whose duty it is as such officer, to take, receive, keep or expend any property on behalf of the Government, or to make any survey, assessment or contract on behalf of the Government, or to execute any revenue-process, or to investigate, or to report, on any matter affecting the pecuniary interests of the Government, or to make, authenticate or keep any document relating to the pecuniary interests of the Government, or to prevent the infraction of any law for the protection of the pecuniary interests of the Government.

Every officer whose duty it is, as such officer, to take, receive, keep or expend any property, to make any survey or assessment or to levy any rate or tax for any secular common purpose of any village, town or district, or to make, authenticate or keep any document for the ascertaining of the rights of the people of any village, town or district.
Every person who holds any office in virtue of which he is empowered to prepare, publish, maintain or revise an electoral roll or to conduct an election or part of an election.
Every person in the service or pay of the Government or remunerated by fees or commission for the performance of any public duty by the Government.

Every person in the service or pay of a local authority, a corporation established by or under a Central, Provincial or State Act or a Government company as defined in section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956 (1 of 1956).
Persons falling under any of the above descriptions are public servants, whether appointed by the Government or not.

Wherever the words “public servant” occur, they shall be understood of every person who is in actual possession of the situation of a public servant, whatever legal defect there may be in his right to hold that situation.

The word “election” denotes an election for the purpose of selecting members of any legislative, municipal or other public authority, of whatever character, the method of selection to which is by, or under, any law prescribed as by election.

23.heading: “Wrongful gain”.
23.canonical_text: This section defines 'wrongful gain' as gain by unlawful means of property to which one is not legally entitled, and 'wrongful loss' as loss by unlawful means of property to which one is legally entitled. It further clarifies that gaining wrongfully includes retaining or acquiring wrongfully, and losing wrongfully includes being wrongfully kept out of or deprived of property.

27.heading: Property in possession of wife, clerk or servant.
27.canonical_text: This section defines when property held by a person's wife, clerk, or servant is considered to be in that person's possession for the purposes of the Code, clarifying that temporary or occasional employment qualifies one as a clerk or servant.

28.canonical_text: This section defines 'counterfeit' as causing one thing to resemble another with the intent to deceive or knowing that deception is likely, and includes clarifications and a presumption regarding intent.

39.heading: “Voluntarily”.
39.canonical_text: This section defines when a person is said to cause an effect "voluntarily," which occurs when they cause it by means they intended to cause it, or by means they knew or had reason to believe were likely to cause it.

53A.heading: Construction of reference to transportation.
53A.canonical_text: This section provides rules for construing references to "transportation" in other laws, specifying that "transportation for life" should be read as "imprisonment for life" and references to "transportation for a term" should be deemed omitted. It also specifies how offenders sentenced to transportation for a term before the 1955 amendment should be treated.

ingredients.text: Any reference to “transportation for life” in any other law for the time being in force or in any instrument or order having effect by virtue of any such law or of any enactment repealed shall be construed as a reference to “imprisonment for life”.
Any reference to “transportation for a term” or to “transportation for any shorter term” (by whatever name called) in any other law for the time being in force shall be deemed to have been omitted.

In every case in which a sentence of transportation for a term has been passed before the commencement of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1955 (26 of 1955), the offender shall be dealt with in the same manner as if sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for the same term.

status.note: Rep. by s.117 and the Sch., ibid. (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

60.heading: Sentence may be (in certain cases of imprisonment) wholly or partly rigorous of simple.
60.canonical_text: This section grants courts the discretion to determine whether imprisonment, when it can be of either description, should be wholly rigorous, wholly simple, or partly rigorous and partly simple.

ingredients.text: An offender is punishable with imprisonment which may be of either description.
The Court which sentences such offender is competent to direct in the sentence the nature of such imprisonment.
The direction may be that such imprisonment shall be wholly rigorous.
The direction may be that such imprisonment shall be wholly simple.
The direction may be that any part of such imprisonment shall be rigorous and the rest simple.

61.heading: [Repealed.].
61.canonical_text: This section, which previously dealt with the sentence of forfeiture of property, has been repealed by the Indian Penal Code (Amendment) Act, 1921.

status.note: Rep. by the Indian Penal Code (Amendment) Act, 1921 (16 of 1921), s. 4.

62.heading: [Repealed.].
62.canonical_text: This section, concerning forfeiture of property for offenders punishable with death, transportation, or imprisonment, has been repealed by section 4 ibid.

ingredients.text: The forfeiture was in respect of offenders punishable with death, transportation or imprisonment.

status.note: Rep. by s. 4 ibid.

63.heading: Amount of fine.
63.canonical_text: If no maximum fine is specified, the amount of fine is unlimited but must not be excessive.

ingredients.text: no sum is expressed to which a fine may extend
the amount of fine to which the offender is liable is unlimited
shall not be excessive

64.heading: Sentence of imprisonment for non-payment of fine.
64.canonical_text: A court may direct that an offender, sentenced to a fine for an offence punishable by imprisonment and/or fine, shall suffer additional imprisonment for a certain term in default of fine payment.

ingredients.text: An offender is sentenced to a fine.
The offence is punishable with imprisonment as well as fine.
The offence is punishable with imprisonment or fine, or with fine only.
The Court directs that, in default of payment of the fine, the offender shall suffer imprisonment for a certain term.
The imprisonment for default of fine payment shall be in excess of any other imprisonment to which the offender may have been sentenced.
The imprisonment for default of fine payment shall be in excess of any other imprisonment to which the offender may be liable under a commutation of a sentence.

65.heading: Limit to imprisonment for non-payment of fine, when imprisonment and fine awardable.
65.canonical_text: This section limits the term of imprisonment for non-payment of a fine to one-fourth of the maximum imprisonment term for an offence, provided the offence is punishable by both imprisonment and fine.

ingredients.text: The Court directs the offender to be imprisoned in default of payment of a fine.
The term of imprisonment for non-payment of a fine shall not exceed one-fourth of the term of imprisonment which is the maximum fixed for the offence.
The offence is punishable with imprisonment as well as fine.

66.heading: Description of imprisonment for non-payment of fine.
66.canonical_text: The type of imprisonment imposed by the Court for non-payment of a fine can be any type applicable to the original offence.

ingredients.text: The Court imposes imprisonment.
Imprisonment is for default of payment of a fine.
The description of imprisonment may be of any description to which the offender might have been sentenced for the offence.

67.heading: Imprisonment for non-payment of fine, when offence punishable with fine only.
67.canonical_text: This section specifies that if an offence is punishable with fine only, the imprisonment for non-payment of fine shall be simple and outlines the maximum terms of such imprisonment based on the fine amount.

ingredients.text: The offence must be punishable with fine only.
The imprisonment which the Court imposes in default of payment of the fine shall be simple.
If the amount of the fine does not exceed fifty rupees, the term of imprisonment for default of payment shall not exceed two months.
If the amount of the fine does not exceed one hundred rupees, the term of imprisonment for default of payment shall not exceed four months.
In any other case (where the fine exceeds one hundred rupees), the term of imprisonment for default of payment shall not exceed six months.

68.heading: Imprisonment to terminate on payment of fine.
68.canonical_text: Imprisonment imposed for non-payment of a fine shall end when the fine is either paid or collected through legal process.

ingredients.text: The imprisonment is imposed in default of payment of a fine.
The fine is paid.
The fine is levied by process of law.

69.heading: Termination of imprisonment on payment of proportional part of fine.
69.canonical_text: Imprisonment in default of fine payment terminates if a proportional part of the fine is paid or levied, such that the imprisonment already served is not less than proportional to the remaining unpaid fine.

ingredients.text: A proportion of the fine is paid or levied before the expiration of the term of imprisonment fixed in default of payment.
The term of imprisonment suffered in default of payment is not less than proportional to the part of the fine still unpaid.

70.heading: Fine leviable within six years, of during imprisonment. Death not to discharge property from liability.
70.canonical_text: This section specifies the timeframe for levying unpaid fines and clarifies that an offender's death does not discharge property from liability for debts.

ingredients.text: A fine, or any unpaid part thereof, may be levied within six years after the passing of the sentence.
If the offender is liable to imprisonment for a period longer than six years, the fine may be levied at any time before that imprisonment period expires.
The death of an offender does not discharge from liability any property that would, after their death, be legally liable for their debts.

71.heading: Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences.
71.canonical_text: This section limits the punishment for an offender when an act constitutes multiple offenses or when several acts combine to form a different offense, preventing punishment for more than one offense or a more severe punishment than for any single offense, unless expressly provided.

ingredients.text: Anything which is an offence is made up of parts, any of which parts is itself an offence.
The offender shall not be punished with the punishment of more than one of such his offences, unless it be so expressly provided.
Anything is an offence falling within two or more separate definitions of any law in force for the time being by which offences are defined or punished.
Several acts, of which one or more than one would by itself or themselves constitute an offence, constitute, when combined, a different offence.
The offender shall not be punished with a more severe punishment than the Court which tries him could award for any one of such offences.

72.heading: Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, the judgment stating that is doubtful of which.
72.canonical_text: This section outlines the sentencing rule when a person is found guilty of one of several specified offences, but it is uncertain which specific offence they committed, mandating punishment for the offence with the lowest penalty if punishments differ.

ingredients.text: A judgment is given that a person is guilty of one of several offences specified in the judgment.
It is doubtful of which of these specified offences the person is guilty.

72.punishment: The offender shall be punished for the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided if the same punishment is not provided for all.

73.heading: Solitary confinement.
73.canonical_text: A court may order solitary confinement as part of a rigorous imprisonment sentence, provided the total solitary confinement does not exceed three months and adheres to a specified scale based on the total imprisonment term.

ingredients.text: Any person is convicted of an offence for which the Court has power to sentence him to rigorous imprisonment under this Code.
The Court may, by its sentence, order that the offender shall be kept in solitary confinement.
Solitary confinement must be for any portion or portions of the imprisonment to which the offender is sentenced.
If the term of imprisonment shall not exceed six months, solitary confinement must not exceed one month.
If the term of imprisonment shall exceed six months and shall not exceed one year, solitary confinement must not exceed two months.
If the term of imprisonment shall exceed one year, solitary confinement must not exceed three months.

74.heading: Limit of solitary confinement.
74.canonical_text: This section sets limits on the duration and frequency of solitary confinement during the execution of a sentence.

ingredients.text: Solitary confinement shall in no case exceed fourteen days at a time.
When the imprisonment awarded exceeds three months, solitary confinement shall not exceed seven days in any one month of the whole imprisonment awarded.

75.heading: Enhanced punishment for certain offences under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII after previous conviction.
75.canonical_text: This section provides for enhanced punishment for a person who, having been previously convicted in India for certain serious offences under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII, commits a subsequent similar offence under those chapters.

ingredients.text: The previous conviction was for an offence punishable under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII of this Code.
The previous offence was punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term of three years or upwards.
The subsequent offence is punishable under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII of this Code.
The subsequent offence is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term of three years or upwards.

75.punishment: imprisonment for life, or to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years

76.heading: Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law.
76.canonical_text: An act is not an offence if it is done by a person who is bound by law to do it, or who, due to a mistake of fact and in good faith, believes themselves to be bound by law to do it, provided it is not due to a mistake of law.

ingredients.text: The act is done by a person who is bound by law to do it.
The act is done by a person who believes himself to be bound by law to do it.
The belief is by reason of a mistake of fact.
The belief is not by reason of a mistake of law.

77.heading: Act of Judge when acting judicially.
77.canonical_text: Nothing is an offence if done by a Judge when acting judicially in the exercise of any power which is, or which in good faith he believes to be, given to him by law.

ingredients.text: The act is done by a Judge.
The Judge is acting judicially.
The act is in the exercise of any power which is given to him by law.
The act is in the exercise of any power which the Judge in good faith believes to be given to him by law.

78.heading: Act done pursuant to the judgment or order of Court.
78.canonical_text: An act done in pursuance of or warranted by a Court's judgment or order, while that order remains in force, is not an offence if the person doing the act in good faith believes the Court had jurisdiction, even if the Court lacked jurisdiction.

ingredients.text: The act is done in pursuance of, or is warranted by, the judgment or order of a Court of Justice.
The person doing the act in good faith believes that the Court had jurisdiction to pass such judgment or order.

79.heading: Act done by a person justified, or by mistake of fact believing himself justified, by law.
79.canonical_text: An act is not an offence if done by a person who is justified by law, or who, due to a good faith mistake of fact (not law), believes themselves to be justified by law.

ingredients.text: The act is done by any person who is justified by law.
The act is done by any person who believes himself to be justified by law.

80.heading: Accident in doing a lawful act.
80.canonical_text: An act is not an offence if it is done by accident or misfortune, without criminal intention or knowledge, during a lawful act performed lawfully, by lawful means, and with proper care and caution.

ingredients.text: The act is done by accident or misfortune.
The act is done without any criminal intention.
The act is done without any criminal knowledge.
The act is done in the doing of a lawful act.
The act is done in a lawful manner.
The act is done by lawful means.
The act is done with proper care and caution.

81.heading: Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm.
81.canonical_text: An act likely to cause harm is not an offence if done without criminal intent and in good faith to prevent other harm to person or property, provided the harm to be prevented was of such a nature and so imminent as to justify the risk.

ingredients.text: The act is done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause harm.
The act is done without any criminal intention to cause harm.
The act is done in good faith.
The act is done for the purpose of preventing or avoiding other harm to person or property.
The harm to be prevented or avoided was of such a nature and so imminent as to justify or excuse the risk of doing the act with the knowledge that it was likely to cause harm.

82.heading: Act of a child under seven years of age.
82.canonical_text: An act done by a child under seven years of age is not considered an offence.

ingredients.text: The act is done by a child.
The child is under seven years of age.

83.heading: Act of a child above seven and under twelve of immature understanding.
83.canonical_text: This section states that an act done by a child between seven and twelve years of age is not an offence if the child has not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge the nature and consequences of their conduct.

ingredients.text: The act is done by a child.
The child is above seven years of age.
The child is under twelve years of age.
The child has not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge of the nature and consequences of his conduct on that occasion.

84.heading: Act of a person of unsound mind.
84.canonical_text: An act is not an offence if committed by a person who, due to unsoundness of mind at the time of the act, is incapable of understanding its nature or that it is wrong or unlawful.

ingredients.text: The act is done by a person.
At the time of doing the act, the person is of unsound mind.
By reason of unsoundness of mind, the person is incapable of knowing the nature of the act.
By reason of unsoundness of mind, the person is incapable of knowing that the act is wrong.
By reason of unsoundness of mind, the person is incapable of knowing that the act is contrary to law.

85.heading: Act of a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication caused against his will.
85.canonical_text: An act is not an offence if committed by a person who, due to involuntary intoxication, is incapable of understanding the nature of the act or its wrongfulness/illegality.

ingredients.text: The person is, at the time of doing the act, intoxicated.
By reason of intoxication, the person is incapable of knowing the nature of the act.
By reason of intoxication, the person is incapable of knowing that the act is wrong.
By reason of intoxication, the person is incapable of knowing that the act is contrary to law.
The thing which intoxicated the person was administered to them without their knowledge.
The thing which intoxicated the person was administered to them against their will.

86.heading: Offence requiring a particular intent or knowledge committed by one who is intoxicated.
86.canonical_text: This section addresses liability for an act committed while intoxicated, where the act requires a particular knowledge or intent, treating the intoxicated person as if they had the knowledge they would have had if sober, unless the intoxication was involuntary.

ingredients.text: The act done is not an offence unless done with a particular knowledge or intent.
A person does the act in a state of intoxication.
The person shall be liable to be dealt with as if he had the same knowledge as he would have had if he had not been intoxicated.
The thing which intoxicated him was administered to him without his knowledge or against his will.

87.heading: Act not intended and not known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, done by consent.
87.canonical_text: An act is not an offence if it is not intended or known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, and is done with the consent of a person over eighteen years of age, even if harm is caused.

ingredients.text: The act is not intended to cause death.
The act is not intended to cause grievous hurt.
The person harmed is above eighteen years of age.
The person has given consent, whether express or implied, to suffer that harm.
The person has consented to take the risk of that harm.

88.heading: Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit.
88.canonical_text: An act not intended to cause death is not an offence if done in good faith for a person's benefit with their consent to suffer or risk harm.

ingredients.text: The act is not intended to cause death.
The act is done for the benefit of the person.
The act is done in good faith.
The person has given consent, whether express or implied, to suffer that harm, or to take the risk of that harm.

89.heading: Act done in good faith for benefit of child or insane person, by or by consent of guardian.
89.canonical_text: An act done in good faith for the benefit of a person under twelve years of age or of unsound mind, by or with the consent of their guardian, is not an offence even if it causes or is likely to cause harm, subject to specific limitations regarding death, grievous hurt, and abetment.

ingredients.text: The act is done in good faith.
The act is for the benefit of a person under twelve years of age.
The act is for the benefit of a person of unsound mind.
The act is done by the guardian or other person having lawful charge of that person.
The act is done by consent, either express or implied, of the guardian or other person having lawful charge of that person.
The act is intended by the doer to cause harm to that person.
The act is known by the doer to be likely to cause harm to that person.
The exception shall not extend to the intentional causing of death.
The exception shall not extend to the attempting to cause death.

The exception shall not extend to the doing of anything which the person doing it knows to be likely to cause death, for any purpose other than the preventing of death or grievous hurt, or the curing of any grievous disease or infirmity.
The exception shall not extend to the voluntary causing of grievous hurt, unless it be for the purpose of preventing death or grievous hurt, or the curing of any grievous disease or infirmity.
The exception shall not extend to the attempting to cause grievous hurt, unless it be for the purpose of preventing death or grievous hurt, or the curing of any grievous disease or infirmity.
The exception shall not extend to the abetment of any offence, to the committing of which offence it would not extend.

90.heading: Consent known to be given under fear or misconception.
90.canonical_text: This section defines when consent is not valid under the Code, specifically if it is given under fear of injury, misconception of fact (and the actor knows this), by a person of unsound mind or intoxicated person unable to understand its nature and consequences, or by a child under twelve years of age.

ingredients.text: The consent is given by a person under fear of injury.
The consent is given by a person under a misconception of fact.
The person doing the act knows, or has reason to believe, that the consent was given in consequence of such fear or misconception.
The consent is given by a person who, from unsoundness of mind, or intoxication, is unable to understand the nature and consequence of that to which he gives his consent.
The consent is given by a person who is under twelve years of age, unless the contrary appears from the context.

91.heading: Exclusion of acts which are offences independently of harm caused.

92.heading: Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent.
92.canonical_text: An act causing harm, done in good faith for a person's benefit without their consent, is not an offence if consent cannot be obtained due to impossibility or incapacity, and no guardian is available. This exception does not apply to acts intentionally causing or attempting death, acts known to be likely to cause death for purposes other than preventing death/grievous hurt/curing grievous disease, acts voluntarily causing or attempting hurt for purposes other than preventing death/hurt, or abetment of such offences. Mere pecuniary benefit is not considered a benefit.

ingredients.text: The act is done for the benefit of that person.
The act is done in good faith.
The act is done without that person's consent.
It is impossible for that person to signify consent OR that person is incapable of giving consent.
The person doing the act knows it is likely to cause death, AND the purpose is not preventing death, grievous hurt, or curing grievous disease or infirmity.
The act is an abetment of an offence to which this exception would not extend.
The benefit is not merely pecuniary.

93.heading: Communication made in good faith.
93.canonical_text: A communication made in good faith for the benefit of a person, which causes harm to that person, is not an offence.

ingredients.text: The communication is made in good faith.
The communication causes harm to the person to whom it is made.
The communication is made for the benefit of the person to whom it is made.

94.heading: Act to which a person is compelled by threats.
94.canonical_text: This section provides an exception to criminal liability for acts committed under compulsion by threats, specifically when the threat reasonably causes apprehension of instant death, provided the person did not voluntarily place themselves in the situation. This exception does not apply to murder or state offences punishable by death.

ingredients.text: An act is done by a person who is compelled to do it by threats.
The threats, at the time of doing the act, reasonably cause the apprehension that instant death to that person will otherwise be the consequence.
The person doing the act did not of his own accord place himself in the situation by which he became subject to such constraint.
The person doing the act did not from a reasonable apprehension of harm to himself short of instant death place himself in the situation by which he became subject to such constraint.
The act is not murder.
The act is not an offence against the State punishable with death.

A person who, of his own accord, or by reason of a threat of being beaten, joins a gang of dacoits, knowing their character, is not entitled to the benefit of this exception if compelled by associates to do an offence.
A person seized by a gang of dacoits, and forced, by threat of instant death, to do a thing which is an offence by law, is entitled to the benefit of this exception.

95.heading: Act causing slight harm.
95.canonical_text: An act causing harm is not an offence if the harm is so slight that no person of ordinary sense and temper would complain of it.

ingredients.text: The act causes harm, or is intended to cause harm, or is known to be likely to cause harm.
No person of ordinary sense and temper would complain of such harm.

96.heading: Things done in private defence.
96.canonical_text: Acts done in the exercise of the right of private defence are not considered offences.

ingredients.text: The act is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.

97.heading: Right of private defence of the body and of property.
97.canonical_text: Every person has a right to defend their own body, the body of any other person, and property (movable or immovable) against certain offences or attempts thereof, subject to restrictions in section 99.

ingredients.text: Every person has a right to defend

His own body
the body of any other person
against any offence affecting the human body
The property, whether movable or immovable, of himself or of any other person
against any act which is an offence falling under the defintion of theft
against any act which is an offence falling under the defintion of robbery
against any act which is an offence falling under the defintion of mischief
against any act which is an offence falling under the defintion of criminal trespass
or which is an attempt to commit theft
or which is an attempt to commit robbery
or which is an attempt to commit mischief
or which is an attempt to commit criminal trespass

98.heading: Right of private defence against the act of a person of unsound mind. etc.
98.canonical_text: This section establishes that the right of private defence is available against an act that would otherwise be an offence, even if the person committing the act is not legally culpable due to reasons such as youth, unsoundness of mind, intoxication, or misconception.

ingredients.text: An act is committed which would otherwise be a certain offence.
The act is not an offence due to the youth of the person doing that act.
The act is not an offence due to the want of maturity of understanding of the person doing that act.
The act is not an offence due to the unsoundness of mind of the person doing that act.
The act is not an offence due to the intoxication of the person doing that act.
The act is not an offence due to any misconception on the part of the person doing that act.
Every person has the same right of private defence against that act.
The right of private defence is the same as if the act were that offence.

99.heading: Acts against which there is no right of private defence.
99.canonical_text: This section defines circumstances where the right of private defence does not exist, primarily when an act by a public servant (or by their direction) does not cause apprehension of death or grievous hurt, when there is time to seek public authority protection, or when the defence exceeds necessary harm. It also clarifies conditions regarding knowledge of the public servant's status or direction.

ingredients.text: The act does not reasonably cause the apprehension of death or of grievous hurt.
The act is done or attempted to be done by a public servant.
The public servant is acting in good faith.
The public servant is acting under colour of his office.
The act is done or attempted to be done by the direction of a public servant.
The public servant giving the direction is acting in good faith.
The public servant giving the direction is acting under colour of his office.
There is time to have recourse to protection of the public authorities.
The right of private defence extends to inflicting more harm than is necessary for the purpose of defence.
The person knows or has reason to believe that the person doing the act is a public servant.
The person knows or has reason to believe that the person doing the act is acting by the direction of a public servant.
The person doing the act states the authority under which he acts.
The person doing the act has authority in writing and produces such authority if demanded.

100.heading: When the right of private defence of the body extends to causing death.
100.canonical_text: This section specifies the conditions under which the right of private defence of the body extends to voluntarily causing death or any other harm to the assailant.

ingredients.text: The right of private defence of the body extends to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the assailant.
The right is exercised under the restrictions mentioned in the last preceding section.
The offence which occasions the exercise of the right is an assault that may reasonably cause the apprehension that death will otherwise be the consequence of such assault.
The offence which occasions the exercise of the right is an assault that may reasonably cause the apprehension that grievous hurt will otherwise be the consequence of such assault.

The offence which occasions the exercise of the right is an assault with the intention of wrongfully confining a person, under circumstances which may reasonably cause him to apprehend that he will be unable to have recourse to the public authorities for his release.

The offence which occasions the exercise of the right is an act of throwing or administering acid or an attempt to throw or administer acid which may reasonably cause the apprehension that grievous hurt will otherwise be the consequence of such act.

101.heading: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death.
101.canonical_text: This section specifies that if an offence is not among those listed in the preceding section, the right of private defence of the body does not permit causing death but does allow causing any harm other than death, subject to the restrictions in section 99.

ingredients.text: The offence is not of any of the descriptions enumerated in the last preceding section.
The right of private defence of the body does not extend to the voluntary causing of death to the assailant.
The right of private defence of the body extends to the voluntary causing to the assailant of any harm other than death.

102.heading: Commencement and continuance of the right of private defence of the body.
102.canonical_text: The right of private defence of the body commences with a reasonable apprehension of danger from an attempt or threat to commit an offence, and continues as long as that apprehension persists.

ingredients.text: The right of private defence of the body commences as soon as a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body arises from an attempt or threat to commit the offence though the offence may not have been committed.
The right of private defence of the body continues as long as such apprehension of danger to the body continues.

103.heading: When the right of private defence of property extends to causing death.
103.canonical_text: The right of private defence of property extends to causing death or other harm to a wrong-doer, subject to Section 99 restrictions, if the offence committed or attempted falls under specific enumerated categories.

ingredients.text: The right of private defence of property extends under the restrictions mentioned in section 99.
The right extends to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the wrong-doer.
The offence, the committing of which, or the attempting to commit which, occasions the exercise of the right.
The offence must be of any of the descriptions hereinafter enumerated.
The offence is Mischief by fire committed on any building, tent or vessel, which building, tent or vessel is used as a human dwelling, or as a place for the custody of property.

The offence is Theft, mischief, or house-trespass, under such circumstances as may reasonably cause apprehension that death or grievous hurt will be the consequence, if such right of private defence is not exercised.

In Karnataka, the offence is Mischief by fire or any explosive substance committed on any building, tent or vessel, which building, tent or vessel is used as a human dwelling, or as a place for the custody of property, or as a place of worship.

In Karnataka, the offence is Mischief by fire or any explosive substance committed on any property used or intended to be used for the purpose of Government or any local authority, statutory body or company owned or controlled by Government or railway or any vehicle used or adapted to be used for the carriage of passengers for hire or reward.

104.heading: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death.
104.canonical_text: The right of private defence extends to causing any harm other than death when the offence occasioning its exercise is theft, mischief, or criminal trespass, provided it is not one of the descriptions enumerated in the last preceding section, and is subject to the restrictions mentioned in section 99.

ingredients.text: The offence occasioning the exercise of the right of private defence is criminal trespass.
The offence is not of any of the descriptions enumerated in the last preceding section.
The right of private defence does not extend to the voluntary causing of death.
The right of private defence extends to the voluntary causing to the wrong-doer of any harm other than death.
The right is subject to the restrictions mentioned in section 99.

105.heading: Commencement and continuance of the right of private defence of property.
105.canonical_text: The right of private defence of property commences with a reasonable apprehension of danger and continues for various durations depending on the specific offense, such as theft, robbery, criminal trespass, mischief, or house-breaking by night.

ingredients.text: The right of private defence of property commences when a reasonable apprehension of danger to the property commences.
The right of private defence of property against theft continues till the offender has effected his retreat with the property.
The right of private defence of property against theft continues till the assistance of the public authorities is obtained.
The right of private defence of property against theft continues till the property has been recovered.
The right of private defence of property against robbery continues as long as the offender causes or attempts to cause to any person death or hurt or wrongful restraint.
The right of private defence of property against robbery continues as long as the fear of instant death or of instant hurt or of instant personal restraint continues.
The right of private defence of property against criminal trespass or mischief continues as long as the offender continues in the commission of criminal trespass or mischief.
The right of private defence of property against house-breaking by night continues as long as the house-trespass which has been begun by such house-breaking continues.

106.heading: Right of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent per son.
106.canonical_text: The right of private defence against an assault reasonably causing apprehension of death extends to risking harm to an innocent person if the defender cannot otherwise effectually exercise that right.

ingredients.text: The defender is exercising the right of private defence.
The private defence is against an assault.
The assault reasonably causes the apprehension of death.
The defender cannot effectually exercise that right without risk of harm to an innocent person.
The right of private defence extends to the running of that risk.

108.heading: Abettor.
108.canonical_text: A person abets an offence if they abet either the commission of an offence, or the commission of an act which would be an offence if committed by a legally capable person with the same intention or knowledge as the abettor. This includes abetment of illegal omission, even if the abettor is not bound to do the act. It is not necessary for the abetted act to be committed, or for the abetted person to be legally capable or share the abettor's intention/knowledge. Abetment of an abetment is also an offence. For abetment by conspiracy, it is sufficient if the abettor engages in the conspiracy in pursuance of which the offence is committed, even if they do not concert with the person who commits it.

It is not necessary that the act abetted should be committed.

It is not necessary that the person abetted should be capable by law of committing an offence.
It is not necessary that the person abetted should have the same guilty intention or knowledge as that of the abettor, or any guilty intention or knowledge.
The abetment of an offence is an offence.
The abetment of such an abetment is also an offence.
For abetment by conspiracy, it is not necessary that the abettor should concert the offence with the person who commits it.
For abetment by conspiracy, it is sufficient if the abettor engages in the conspiracy in pursuance of which the offence is committed.

108A.heading: Abetment in Indian of offences outside India.
108A.canonical_text: This section defines that a person abets an offence within the meaning of this Code if, in India, they abet the commission of any act without and beyond India which would constitute an offence if committed in India.

ingredients.text: The act abetted is committed without and beyond India.

109.heading: Punishment of a abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence and when no express provision is made for its punishment.
109.canonical_text: This section provides for the punishment of abetment when the abetted act is committed as a consequence of the abetment, and no specific punishment for such abetment is otherwise provided in the Code.

111.heading: Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done.
111.canonical_text: When an act is abetted and a different act is done, the abettor is liable for the act done if it was a probable consequence of the abetment and committed under the influence of the instigation, or with the aid or in pursuance of the conspiracy which constituted the abetment.

The abettor is liable for the act done, in the same manner and to the same extent as if he had directly abetted it.

112.heading: Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done.
112.canonical_text: This section specifies when an abettor is liable to cumulative punishment for an act abetted and an additional act committed, provided both constitute distinct offences and the abettor is liable for the additional act.

113.heading: Liability of abettor for an effect caused by the act abetted different from that intended by the abettor.
113.canonical_text: An abettor is liable for an effect caused by the abetted act, even if different from the intended effect, provided the abettor knew the abetted act was likely to cause that effect.

The abettor intended to cause a particular effect by abetting the act.
The abetted act causes an effect different from that intended by the abettor.
The abettor knew that the abetted act was likely to cause the different effect that actually occurred.
The abettor is liable for the effect caused.
The abettor's liability is to the same extent as if they had abetted the act with the intention of causing that effect.

114.heading: Abettor present when offence is committed.
114.canonical_text: An abettor who would be liable for punishment if absent, but is present during the commission of the abetted act or offence, shall be deemed to have committed that act or offence.

ingredients.text: That person is present when the act or offence is committed.

115.heading: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life.—if offence not committed.
115.canonical_text: This section prescribes punishment for abetment of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, where the abetted offence is not committed and no specific provision for such abetment exists. 116.heading: Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment.—if offence be not committed.

118.heading: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
118.canonical_text: Whoever, intending or knowing it likely to facilitate a capital or life imprisonment offence, voluntarily conceals the design to commit such offence by act, omission, encryption, or false representation.

Makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design.

118.punishment: If the offence is committed, imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and liable to fine. If the offence is not committed, imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and liable to fine.

119.heading: Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent.
119.canonical_text: A public servant who, with intent to facilitate or knowing it likely to facilitate an offence they are duty-bound to prevent, conceals the design to commit such offence or makes false representations about it.

120.heading: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment.

120A.heading: Definition of criminal conspiracy.
120A.canonical_text: A criminal conspiracy is an agreement between two or more persons to do an illegal act, or a legal act by illegal means, with a specific requirement for an overt act if the agreement is not to commit an offence.

If the agreement is not to commit an offence, some act besides the agreement must be done by one or more parties to such agreement in pursuance thereof.
It is immaterial whether the illegal act is the ultimate object of such agreement, or is merely incidental to that object.

120B.heading: Punishment of criminal conspiracy.
120B.canonical_text: This section prescribes the punishment for criminal conspiracy, differentiating between conspiracies to commit serious offences (punishable with death, life imprisonment, or rigorous imprisonment for two years or more) and conspiracies to commit less serious offences. For serious offences, the punishment is the same as for abetment of that offence, provided no specific provision exists in the Code. For less serious offences, the punishment is imprisonment up to six months, or a fine, or both.

121.heading: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against the Government of India.
121.canonical_text: Whoever wages war, attempts to wage war, or abets the waging of war against the Government of India, shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life and fine.

124.heading: Assaulting President. Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any lawful power.

124A.heading: Sedition.

125.heading: Waging war against any Asiatic power in alliance with the Government of India.

126.heading: Committing depredation on territories of power at peace with the Government of India.

128.heading: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of State or war to escape.
128.canonical_text: A public servant having custody of a State prisoner or prisoner of war who voluntarily allows such prisoner to escape from confinement.

129.heading: Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape.
129.canonical_text: A public servant having custody of a State prisoner or prisoner of war, who negligently allows the prisoner to escape from confinement, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to three years and a fine.

130.heading: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner.
130.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who knowingly aids, assists, rescues, harbours, conceals, or resists the recapture of a State prisoner or prisoner of war escaping or having escaped from lawful custody. Punishment includes imprisonment for life or up to ten years, and a fine.

The accused harbours or conceals any such prisoner who has escaped from lawful custody.

A State prisoner or prisoner of war, permitted to be at large on parole within certain limits in India, is said to escape from lawful custody if they go beyond those limits.

131.heading: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty.

135.heading: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman.

141.heading: Unlawful assembly.
141.canonical_text: An assembly of five or more persons is designated an “unlawful assembly” if their common object falls under one of five specified categories, including overawing government or public servants, resisting law, committing offences, taking property or rights by force, or compelling actions by force. An assembly not initially unlawful may become so subsequently.

ingredients.text: The common object is to overawe by criminal force, or show of criminal force, the Central or any State Government or Parliament or the Legislature of any State, or any public servant in the exercise of the lawful power of such public servant.
The common object is to resist the execution of any law, or of any legal process.
The common object is to commit any mischief or criminal trespass, or other offence.

The common object is, by means of criminal force, or show of criminal force, to any person, to take or obtain possession of any property, or to deprive any person of the enjoyment of a right of way, or of the use of water or other incorporeal right of which he is in possession or enjoyment, or to enforce any right or supposed right.
The common object is, by means of criminal force, or show of criminal force, to compel any person to do what he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do what he is legally entitled to do.
An assembly which was not unlawful when it assembled, may subsequently become an unlawful assembly.

147.canonical_text: Punishment for being guilty of rioting.

147.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

148.heading: Rioting, armed with deadly weapon.
148.canonical_text: This section defines the offense of rioting while armed with a deadly weapon or an object likely to cause death, and prescribes its punishment.

ingredients.text: The accused is armed with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death.

148.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both

149.heading: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object.
149.canonical_text: This section establishes that every member of an unlawful assembly is guilty of an offence committed by any member of that assembly if the offence was committed in prosecution of the common object, or was known by the members to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object.

ingredients.text: An offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly.
The offence is committed in prosecution of the common object of that assembly.
The offence is such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object.
The person was a member of the same unlawful assembly at the time of the committing of that offence.
Every such person is guilty of that offence.

150.heading: Hiring, or conniving at hiring, of persons to join unlawful assembly.
150.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who hires, engages, employs, promotes, or connives at the hiring, engagement, or employment of any person to join or become a member of an unlawful assembly.

ingredients.text: Whoever hires or engages, or employs, or promotes, or connives at the hiring, engagement or employment
of any person
to join or become a member of any unlawful assembly

150.punishment: shall be punishable as a member of such unlawful assembly, and for any offence which may be committed by any such person as a member of such unlawful assembly in pursuance of such hiring, engagement or employment, in the same manner as if he had been a member of such unlawful assembly, or himself had committed such offence.

151.heading: Knowingly joining or continuing in assembly of five or more persons after it has been commanded to disperse.
151.canonical_text: This section penalizes individuals who knowingly join or continue in an assembly of five or more persons, likely to disturb public peace, after it has been lawfully commanded to disperse.

ingredients.text: The assembly consists of five or more persons.
The assembly is likely to cause a disturbance of the public peace.
The assembly has been lawfully commanded to disperse.

151.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both

152.heading: Assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc.
152.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who assaults, threatens, obstructs, or uses criminal force against a public servant while they are performing their duty to disperse an unlawful assembly or suppress a riot or affray.

ingredients.text: Whoever assaults or threatens to assault any public servant
Whoever obstructs or attempts to obstruct any public servant
Whoever uses, or threatens, or attempts to use criminal force to such public servant
The public servant is in the discharge of his duty as such public servant
The public servant is endeavouring to disperse an unlawful assembly
The public servant is endeavouring to suppress a riot or affray

152.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

153.heading: Wantonly giving provocation, with intent to cause riot— if rioting be committed; if not committed.
153.canonical_text: Whoever malignantly or wantonly gives provocation by an illegal act, intending or knowing it likely to cause rioting, is punished. The punishment varies depending on whether rioting is actually committed.

ingredients.text: A person malignantly or wantonly gives provocation to any person.
The person intends or knows it to be likely that such provocation will cause the offence of rioting to be committed.
The offence of rioting is committed in consequence of such provocation.
The offence of rioting is not committed.

153.punishment: If rioting is committed: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. If rioting is not committed: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

153A.heading: Punishment for knowingly carrying arms in any procession or organizing, or holding or taking part in any mass drill or mass training with arms.
153A.canonical_text: This section punishes individuals who knowingly carry arms in public processions or participate in mass drills/training with arms in public places, in contravention of orders issued under section 144A of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

carries arms

or organizes or holds or takes part in any mass drill or mass training

normalized.definition: articles of any description designed or adapted as weapons for offence or defence and includes firearms, sharp edged weapons, lathis, dandas and sticks

153A.punishment: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees

153B.heading: Imputation, assertions prejudicial to national-integration.
153B.canonical_text: This section defines offences related to making imputations or assertions, by various means, that are prejudicial to national integration, including questioning allegiance to the Constitution, denying citizens' rights based on group affiliation, or causing disharmony, and prescribes punishment.

ingredients.text: Whoever, by words either spoken or written or by signs or by visible representations or otherwise

normalized.communication_method: spoken, written, signs, visible representations, otherwise

that any class of persons cannot, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established or uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India

normalized.target_group_characteristic: religious, racial, language, regional, caste, community

153B.punishment: imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both

154.heading: Owner or occupier of land on which an unlawful assembly is held.
154.canonical_text: This section penalizes the owner, occupier, or interested party of land, or their agent/manager, if an unlawful assembly or riot occurs on their land, and they, knowing or having reason to believe it would occur, fail to give notice to the police, fail to prevent it (if believed imminent), or fail to disperse/suppress it once it has taken place.

ingredients.text: An unlawful assembly or riot takes place.
The accused is the owner or occupier of the land, or a person having or claiming an interest in such land, or their agent or manager.
The accused knows that such offence is being or has been committed, or has reason to believe it is likely to be committed.
The accused does not give the earliest notice thereof in their power to the principal officer at the nearest police-station.
In the case of having reason to believe that it was about to be committed, the accused does not use all lawful means in their power to prevent it.
In the event of the unlawful assembly or riot taking place, the accused does not use all lawful means in their power to disperse or suppress it.

154.punishment: fine not exceeding one thousand rupees

155.heading: Liability of person for whose benefit riot is committed.
155.canonical_text: A person for whose benefit a riot is committed is liable to a fine if they, their agent, or manager, having reason to believe the riot or unlawful assembly was likely, failed to use lawful means to prevent or suppress it.

ingredients.text: A riot is committed.
The riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of a person.
The person is the owner or occupier of any land respecting which such riot takes place.
The person claims any interest in such land.
The person claims any interest in the subject of any dispute which gave rise to the riot.
The person has accepted or derived any benefit from the riot.
The person or their agent or manager had reason to believe that such riot was likely to be committed.
The person or their agent or manager had reason to believe that the unlawful assembly by which such riot was committed was likely to be held.
The person or their agent or manager did not use all lawful means in their power to prevent such assembly or riot from taking place.
The person or their agent or manager did not use all lawful means in their power for suppressing and dispersing the same (assembly or riot).

156.heading: Liablility of agent of owner or occupier for whose benefit riot is committed.
156.canonical_text: An agent or manager is liable to a fine if a riot occurs for the benefit of their principal (owner/occupier of land, claimant of interest, or beneficiary of the riot), and the agent/manager, having reason to believe the riot or unlawful assembly was likely, failed to use all lawful means to prevent, suppress, or disperse it.

ingredients.text: A riot is committed.
The riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of a person who is the owner or occupier of any land respecting which such riot takes place.
The riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of a person who claims any interest in such land.
The riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of a person who claims any interest in the subject of any dispute which gave rise to the riot.
The riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of a person who has accepted or derived any benefit therefrom.
The agent or manager of such person had reason to believe that such riot was likely to be committed.
The agent or manager of such person had reason to believe that the unlawful assembly by which such riot was committed was likely to be held.
The agent or manager did not use all lawful means in his power to prevent such riot or assembly from taking place.
The agent or manager did not use all lawful means in his power for suppressing and dispersing the same.

157.heading: Harbouring persons hired for an unlawful assembly.
157.canonical_text: Whoever harbours, receives or assembles persons in their premises, knowing they are hired or about to be hired to join an unlawful assembly, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: Whoever harbours, receives or assembles persons
in any house or premises in his occupation or charge, or under his control
knowing that such persons have been hired, engaged or employed, or are about to be hired, engaged or employed
to join or become members of an unlawful assembly

157.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both

158.heading: Being hired to take part in an unlawful assembly or riot; or to go armed.
158.canonical_text: This section defines two offenses: first, being hired or attempting to be hired to participate in or assist with acts specified in section 141; and second, being so hired and going armed or offering to go armed with a deadly weapon or an object likely to cause death.

ingredients.text: Whoever is engaged, or hired, or offers or attempts to be hired or engaged
to do or assist in doing any of the acts specified in section 141
whoever, being so engaged or hired as aforesaid
goes armed, or engages or offers to go armed
with any deadly weapon or with anything which used as a weapon of offence is likely to cause death

158.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

159.heading: Affray.
159.canonical_text: When two or more persons fight in a public place and disturb the public peace, they commit an affray.

ingredients.text: two or more persons
by fighting
in a public place
disturb the public peace

160.heading: Punishment for committing affray.
160.canonical_text: Committing an affray is punishable by imprisonment, fine, or both.
160.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees, or with both

161.heading: [Repealed.].
161.canonical_text: Section 161, concerning a public servant taking gratification other than legal remuneration in respect of an official act, was repealed by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

status.note: Repealed by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (49 of 1988), s. 31.

162.canonical_text: Original content regarding taking gratification to influence a public servant, now repealed.

in order, by corrupt or illegal means, to influence a public servant

status.note: Rep. by s. 31, ibid.

163.canonical_text: This section, which previously addressed taking gratification for the exercise of personal influence with a public servant, has been repealed.

status.note: Repealed by s. 31, ibid. The original content concerned taking a gratification for the exercise of personal influence with a public servant.

164.heading: [Repealed.].
164.canonical_text: This section, which previously outlined punishment for abetment by public servants, has been repealed by section 31, ibid.

status.note: Rep. by s. 31, ibid.

166.heading: Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person.
166.canonical_text: A public servant knowingly disobeys a legal direction regarding their conduct, intending or knowing it likely to cause injury to any person.

ingredients.text: The offender is a public servant.
The offender knowingly disobeys any direction of the law.
The direction of the law pertains to the way the public servant is to conduct himself as such public servant.
The offender intends to cause injury to any person by such disobedience.
The offender knows it to be likely that he will by such disobedience, cause injury to any person.

166.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

166A.heading: Public servant disobeying direction under law.
166A.canonical_text: A public servant commits an offence if they knowingly disobey a direction of law regarding requiring attendance or regulating investigation, or fail to record information about specific cognizable offences.

ingredients.text: The public servant knowingly disobeys any direction of the law which prohibits him from requiring the attendance at any place of any person for the purpose of investigation into an offence or any other matter.
The public servant knowingly disobeys, to the prejudice of any person, any other direction of the law regulating the manner in which he shall conduct such investigation.
The public servant fails to record any information given to him under sub-section (1) of section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).

The information relates to a cognizable offence punishable under section 326A, section 326B, section 354, section 354B, section 370, section 370A, section 376, section 376A, section 376AB, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA, section 376DB, section 376E or section 509.

166A.punishment: rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine

166B.heading: Punishment for non-treatment of victim.
166B.canonical_text: This section prescribes punishment for individuals in charge of hospitals who violate the provisions of section 357C of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

ingredients.text: Whoever, being in charge of a hospital, public or private, whether run by the Central Government, the State Government, local bodies or any other person
contravenes the provisions of section 357C of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974)

166B.punishment: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine or with both

167.heading: Public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury.
167.canonical_text: A public servant charged with preparing or translating a document or electronic record, who frames, prepares, or translates it incorrectly, knowing or believing it to be incorrect, and intending or knowing it likely to cause injury to any person, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: The public servant is charged with the preparation or translation of any document or electronic record.
The public servant frames, prepares, or translates that document or electronic record.
The public servant intends thereby to cause injury to any person.
The public servant knows it to be likely that he may thereby cause injury to any person.

167.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

168.heading: Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade.
168.canonical_text: A public servant who is legally bound not to engage in trade, and does so, shall be punished.
168.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both

169.heading: Public servant unlawfully buying or bidding for property.
169.canonical_text: A public servant who is legally prohibited from purchasing or bidding for certain property, and who proceeds to purchase or bid for that property, either personally or through others, commits an offence. The punishment includes imprisonment, fine, or both, and confiscation of the property if purchased.

ingredients.text: The public servant is legally bound not to purchase or bid for certain property.
The public servant purchases or bids for that property.
The purchase or bid is made either in his own name or in the name of another, or jointly, or in shares with others.

169.punishment: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; and the property, if purchased, shall be confiscated.

170.heading: Personating a public servant.
170.canonical_text: Whoever pretends to hold a public office or falsely personates another public servant, knowing they do not hold such office, and acts under color of such office, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: Whoever pretends to hold any particular office as a public servant
knowing that he does not hold such office
or falsely personates any other person holding such office
and in such assumed character does or attempts to do any act under colour of such office

normalized.action: does or attempts to do act

170.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

171.heading: Failure to keep election accounts.
171.canonical_text: This section punishes individuals who fail to keep accounts of expenses incurred at or in connection with an election, as required by law or rule.

ingredients.text: A person is required by any law for the time being in force or any rule having the force of law to keep accounts of expenses incurred at or in connection with an election.

171.punishment: fine which may extend to five hundred rupees

171B.heading: Bribery.
171B.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of bribery related to electoral rights, covering both the act of giving gratification to induce or reward the exercise of such rights, and the act of accepting gratification as a reward or for inducing the exercise of such rights. It also specifies that declarations of public policy or promises of public action are not offences, and includes deeming provisions for what constitutes giving or accepting gratification.

ingredients.text: A person gives a gratification.
The object is to induce any person to exercise any electoral right.
The object is to reward any person for having exercised any electoral right.
A person accepts a gratification.
The gratification is for inducing any other person to exercise an electoral right.
The gratification is for attempting to induce any other person to exercise an electoral right.
A declaration of public policy shall not be an offence under this section.
A promise of public action shall not be an offence under this section.

171C.heading: Undue influence at elections.
171C.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of undue influence at elections, specifying that it involves voluntarily interfering or attempting to interfere with the free exercise of any electoral right, including through threats of injury or religious inducement, while also clarifying what actions do not constitute such interference.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily interferes or attempts to interfere
with the free exercise of any electoral right
threatens any candidate or voter, or any person in whom a candidate or voter is interested, with injury of any kind
induces or attempts to induce a candidate or voter to believe that he or any person in whom he is interested will become or will be rendered an object of Divine displeasure or of spiritual censure

171D.heading: Personation at elections.
171D.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of personation at an election, which includes applying for a voting paper or voting in another's name or a fictitious name, or voting multiple times, and abetting such acts. It also provides an exception for authorized proxy voting.

ingredients.text: Whoever at an election applies for a voting paper or votes in the name of any other person, whether living or dead.
Whoever at an election applies for a voting paper or votes in a fictitious name.
Whoever, having voted once at an election, applies at the same election for a voting paper in his own name.
Whoever abets, procures or attempts to procure the voting by any person in any such way (as described above).
Nothing in this section shall apply to a person who has been authorised to vote as proxy for an elector under any law for the time being in force in so far as he votes as a proxy for such elector.

171E.heading: Punishment for bribery.
171E.canonical_text: This section prescribes the punishment for the offence of bribery, including a specific punishment for bribery by treating, which is defined as gratification consisting of food, drink, entertainment, or provision.

ingredients.text: The gratification consists in food, drink, entertainment, or provision.

171E.punishment: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both.

171F.heading: Punishment for undue influence or personation at an election.
171F.canonical_text: This section prescribes punishment for committing undue influence or personation at an election.

ingredients.text: Whoever commits the offence of undue influence at an election
Whoever commits the offence of personation at an election

171F.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year or with fine, or with both

171G.heading: False statement in connection with an election.
171G.canonical_text: Whoever, with intent to affect an election's result, makes or publishes a false statement of fact concerning a candidate's personal character or conduct, knowing or believing it to be false or not believing it to be true, shall be punished with fine.

ingredients.text: Whoever with intent to affect the result of an election
