171H.heading: Illegal payments in connection with an election.
171H.canonical_text: Prohibits any person from incurring or authorizing expenses without a candidate's written authority for promoting or procuring the candidate's election, covering public meetings, advertisements, or other similar activities, punishable by a fine.

ingredients.text: A person incurs or authorises expenses.
Such expenses are incurred without the general or special authority in writing of a candidate.
Such expenses are on account of the holding of any public meeting, or upon any advertisement, circular or publication, or in any other way whatsoever.
The purpose of such expenses is promoting or procuring the election of such candidate.

171H.punishment: fine which may extend to five hundred rupees

172.heading: Absconding to avoid service of summons of other proceeding.
172.canonical_text: This section criminalizes absconding to avoid service of a summons, notice, or order issued by a legally competent public servant. It provides for a higher punishment if the document requires attendance in person or by agent, or the production of a document or electronic record in a Court of Justice.

ingredients.text: Whoever absconds
in order to avoid being served
with a summons, notice or order
proceeding from any public servant
legally competent, as such public servant, to issue such summons, notice or order
if the summons or notice or order is to attend in person or by agent

normalized.requirement: attend in person or by agent

ingredients.text: if the summons or notice or order is to produce a document or an electronic record in a Court of Justice

172.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both; or, if the summons or notice or order is to attend in person or by agent, or to produce a document or an electronic record in a Court of Justice, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

173.heading: Preventing service of summons or other proceeding, or preventing publication thereof.
173.canonical_text: This section criminalizes intentionally obstructing the service, affixing, or removal of legal summons, notices, or orders, or the making of proclamations, issued by a competent public servant.

ingredients.text: Whoever intentionally prevents the serving on himself, or on any other person.
The serving is of any summons, notice, or order.
The summons, notice, or order proceeds from any public servant legally competent to issue such summons, notice, or order.
Whoever intentionally prevents the lawful affixing to any place of any such summons, notice, or order.
Whoever intentionally removes any such summons, notice, or order from any place to which it is lawfully affixed.
Whoever intentionally prevents the lawful making of any proclamation.
The proclamation is under the authority of any public servant legally competent to direct such proclamation to be made.

173.punishment: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both; or, if the summons, notice, order or proclamation is to attend in person or by agent, or to produce a document or electronic record in a Court of Justice, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

174.heading: Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant.
174.canonical_text: Whoever, being legally bound to attend in person or by an agent in obedience to a directive from a competent public servant, intentionally omits to attend or departs prematurely, commits an offense.

ingredients.text: The accused is legally bound to attend.
The attendance is in person or by an agent.
The attendance is at a certain place and time.
The attendance is in obedience to a summons, notice, order, or proclamation.
The summons, notice, order, or proclamation proceeds from a public servant.
The public servant is legally competent to issue the summons, notice, order, or proclamation.
The accused intentionally omits to attend at that place or time.
The departure occurs before the time at which it is lawful for him to depart.

174.punishment: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

174A.heading: Non-appearance in response to a proclamatio n under section 82 of Act 2 of 1974.
174A.canonical_text: This section criminalizes the failure to appear at a specified place and time as required by a proclamation issued under section 82(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. A more severe punishment is prescribed if the person is declared a proclaimed offender under section 82(4).

ingredients.text: Whoever fails to appear at the specified place and the specified time.
The appearance is required by a proclamation published under sub-section (1) of section 82 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
A declaration has been made under sub-section (4) of section 82 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, pronouncing him as a proclaimed offender.

174A.punishment: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

175.heading: Omission to produce document to public servant by person legally bound to produce it.
175.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of intentionally omitting to produce or deliver a document or electronic record when legally bound to do so, either to a public servant or a Court of Justice.

ingredients.text: Whoever is legally bound to produce or deliver up any document or electronic record
The person intentionally omits so to produce or deliver up the same
Alternatively, the document or electronic record is to be produced or delivered up to a Court of Justice

175.punishment: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both; or, if the document or electronic record is to be produced or delivered up to a Court of Justice, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

176.heading: Omission to give notice or information to public servant by person legally bound to give it.
176.canonical_text: A person legally bound to provide notice or information to a public servant who intentionally omits to do so in the prescribed manner and time commits an offense.

ingredients.text: Whoever, being legally bound to give any notice or to furnish information on any subject to any public servant, as such,

normalized.action: omits to give notice or furnish information
