normalized.condition: manner and time required by law

176.punishment: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both; or, if the notice or information respects the commission of an offence, or is for preventing an offence, or apprehending an offender, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both; or, if the notice or information is required by an order under sub-section (1) of section 565 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

177.heading: Furnishing false information.
177.canonical_text: Whoever, being legally bound to furnish information to a public servant, provides information on a subject as true, which they know or have reason to believe to be false, commits an offense.

ingredients.text: A person is legally bound to furnish information on any subject to any public servant.
The person knows or has reason to believe the information to be false.
The information which the person is legally bound to give respects the commission of an offence.
The information is required for the purpose of preventing the commission of an offence.
The information is required in order to the apprehension of an offender.

The word “offence” includes any act committed at any place out of India, which, if committed in India, would be punishable under sections 302, 304, 382, 392, 393, 394, 395, 396, 397, 398, 399, 402, 435, 436, 449, 450, 457, 458, 459 and 460.
The word “offender” includes any person who is alleged to have been guilty of any such act.

177.punishment: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both; or, if the information concerns the commission or prevention of an offence, or apprehension of an offender, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

178.heading: Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant to make it.
178.canonical_text: Whoever refuses to bind himself by an oath or affirmation to state the truth, when legally required by a competent public servant, commits an offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever refuses to bind himself by an oath or affirmation to state the truth
when required so to bind himself by a public servant
The public servant must be legally competent to require that he shall so bind himself

178.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

179.heading: Refusing to answer public servant authori sed to question.
179.canonical_text: Whoever, being legally bound to state the truth to a public servant, refuses to answer questions demanded by that public servant in the exercise of their legal powers, commits an offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever is legally bound to state the truth on any subject to any public servant
refuses to answer any question demanded of him touching that subject by such public servant
such public servant is in the exercise of their legal powers

179.punishment: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

180.heading: Refusing to sign statement.
180.canonical_text: This section penalizes any person who refuses to sign a statement made by them, when a legally competent public servant requires them to do so.

ingredients.text: Whoever refuses to sign any statement made by him
when required to sign that statement by a public servant
legally competent to require that he shall sign that statement

180.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

181.heading: False statement on oath or affirmation to public servant or person authorised to administer an oath or affirmation.
181.canonical_text: A person makes a false statement under oath or affirmation to a public servant or authorized person, knowing or believing it to be false, or not believing it to be true.

ingredients.text: The person is legally bound by an oath or affirmation to state the truth on any subject.
The statement is made to a public servant or other person authorized by law to administer such oath or affirmation.
The statement is false.
The person either knows or believes the statement to be false or does not believe it to be true.

181.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

182.heading: False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to the injury of another person.
182.canonical_text: Whoever gives false information to a public servant, knowing or believing it to be false, with the intent or knowledge that it is likely to cause the public servant to act improperly or to use their lawful power to injure or annoy another person.

ingredients.text: The accused gives information to any public servant.
The information is false.
The accused knows or believes the information to be false.
The accused intends to cause the public servant to do or omit anything which such public servant ought not to do or omit if the true state of facts were known by him.

The accused knows it to be likely that the information will cause the public servant to do or omit anything which such public servant ought not to do or omit if the true state of facts were known by him.
The accused knows it to be likely that the information will cause the public servant to use their lawful power to the injury or annoyance of any person.

182.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

183.heading: Resistance to the taking of property by the lawful authority of a public servant.
183.canonical_text: This section penalizes resistance to the lawful taking of property by a public servant, where the offender knows or believes the person is a public servant.

ingredients.text: Whoever offers any resistance
to the taking of any property
by the lawful authority of any public servant
knowing or having reason to believe that he is such public servant

183.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both

184.heading: Obstructing sale of property offered for sale by authority of public servant.
184.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who intentionally obstructs the sale of property offered by the lawful authority of a public servant.

ingredients.text: Whoever intentionally obstructs
any sale of property
offered for sale by the lawful authority of any public servant, as such

184.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both

185.heading: Illegal purchase or bid for property offered for sale by authority of public servant.
185.canonical_text: Whoever, at a sale of property held by the lawful authority of a public servant, purchases or bids for property on behalf of someone known to be legally incapacitated, or bids without intending to fulfill the obligations, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: Whoever purchases or bids for any property
at any sale of property held by the lawful authority of a public servant, as such
on account of any person, whether himself or any other, whom he knows to be under a legal incapacity to purchase that property at that sale
or bids for such property not intending to perform the obligations under which he lays himself by such bidding

185.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both.

186.heading: Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions.
186.canonical_text: Voluntarily obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their public functions.
186.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

187.heading: Omission to assist public servant when bound by law to give assistance.
187.canonical_text: This section penalizes individuals who, being legally bound to assist a public servant in their duty, intentionally fail to do so. An aggravated punishment applies if the assistance was demanded for specific judicial or law enforcement purposes.

ingredients.text: The accused is bound by law to render or furnish assistance to a public servant.
The accused intentionally omits to give such assistance.
Such assistance is demanded by a public servant legally competent to make such demand.
The demand is for the purpose of executing any process lawfully issued by a Court of Justice.
The demand is for the purpose of apprehending a person charged with or guilty of an offence.

187.punishment: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both; and if such assistance be demanded for specific purposes (executing court process, preventing offence, suppressing riot/affray, apprehending offender/escapee), simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

188.heading: Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant.
188.canonical_text: Disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant, where such disobedience causes or tends to cause specific harms or risks.

ingredients.text: The order was promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate such order.
Such disobedience causes or tends to cause obstruction, annoyance or injury, or risk of obstruction, annoyance or injury, to any persons lawfully employed.
Such disobedience causes or tends to cause danger to human life, health or safety, or causes or tends to cause a riot or affray.

188.punishment: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both; and if such disobedience causes or tends to cause danger to human life, health or safety, or causes or tends to cause a riot or affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

189.heading: Threat of injury to public servant.
189.canonical_text: This section penalizes any individual who threatens injury to a public servant or a person connected to them, with the intent to influence the public servant's official duties.

ingredients.text: Whoever holds out any threat of injury
to any public servant
or to any person in whom he believes that public servant to be interested
for the purpose of inducing that public servant to do any act
or to forbear or delay to do any act
connected with the exercise of the public functions of such public servant

189.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

190.heading: Threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant.
190.canonical_text: Threatening injury to a person to prevent them from seeking protection from a public servant.

ingredients.text: Whoever holds out any threat of injury to any person
for the purpose of inducing that person to refrain or desist from making a legal application for protection against any injury
to any public servant legally empowered as such to give such protection, or to cause such protection to be given

190.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both

191.heading: Giving false evidence.
191.canonical_text: Whoever, being legally bound to state the truth or make a declaration, makes a false statement which they know or believe to be false, or do not believe to be true, is said to give false evidence.

ingredients.text: Whoever is legally bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth
Whoever is bound by law to make a declaration upon any subject
makes any statement
the statement is false
the person knows the statement to be false
the person believes the statement to be false
the person does not believe the statement to be true

192.heading: Fabricating false evidence.
192.canonical_text: This section defines the act of 'fabricating false evidence' as causing a false circumstance to exist, or making a false entry or statement in a record or document, with the intent that it appears as evidence in a legal proceeding and causes an erroneous opinion on a material point.

ingredients.text: Whoever causes any circumstance to exist
Whoever makes any false entry in any book or record, or electronic record
Whoever makes any document or electronic record containing a false statement
intending that such circumstance, false entry or false statement may appear in evidence in a judicial proceeding
intending that such circumstance, false entry or false statement may appear in evidence in a proceeding taken by law before a public servant as such
intending that such circumstance, false entry or false statement may appear in evidence before an arbitrator

intending that such circumstance, false entry or false statement, so appearing in evidence, may cause any person who in such proceeding is to form an opinion upon the evidence, to entertain an erroneous opinion touching any point material to the result of such proceeding

193.heading: Punishment for false evidence.
193.canonical_text: This section defines the offense of giving or fabricating false evidence, distinguishing between cases occurring in a judicial proceeding and those in other contexts, and prescribes different punishments accordingly. It also clarifies what constitutes a 'judicial proceeding' or a 'stage of a judicial proceeding'.

ingredients.text: Whoever intentionally gives false evidence
in any stage of a judicial proceeding
or fabricates false evidence
for the purpose of being used in any stage of a judicial proceeding
whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence
in any other case

193.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine (for judicial proceedings); or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine (for any other case).

194.heading: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence.
194.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of giving or fabricating false evidence with the intent or knowledge that it will lead to the conviction of a capital offence, and prescribes punishment, including a more severe punishment if an innocent person is convicted and executed as a result.

ingredients.text: Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence
intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence

normalized.mens_rea: intending or knowing it to be likely

ingredients.text: which is capital by the law for the time being in force in India
if an innocent person be convicted and executed in consequence of such false evidence

normalized.causation: in consequence of such false evidence

194.punishment: Imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and fine; potentially death if an innocent person is convicted and executed.

195.heading: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment.
195.canonical_text: Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence with the intent or knowledge that it will cause a person to be convicted of a non-capital offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for seven years or more, shall be punished as if convicted of that offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence
intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence
the offence is not capital by the law for the time being in force in India
the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term of seven years or upwards

195.punishment: punished as a person convicted of that offence would be liable to be punished

195A.heading: Threatening any person to give false evidence.
195A.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of threatening a person to compel them to give false evidence and prescribes punishments, including enhanced punishment if an innocent person is convicted and sentenced as a result of such false evidence.

ingredients.text: Whoever threatens another.
The threat is with any injury to the person, reputation, or property of the threatened person.
The threat is made with intent to cause that person to give false evidence.
An innocent person is convicted and sentenced in consequence of such false evidence.

195A.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both; if an innocent person is convicted and sentenced to death or imprisonment for more than seven years in consequence of such false evidence, the person who threatens shall be punished with the same punishment and sentence as the innocent person.

196.heading: Using evidence known to be false.
196.canonical_text: Prohibits corruptly using or attempting to use as true or genuine any evidence known to be false or fabricated.

ingredients.text: The person uses or attempts to use evidence.
The person knows the evidence to be false or fabricated.

197.heading: Issuing or signing false certificate.
197.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who issues or signs a certificate, which is legally required or admissible as evidence, knowing or believing it to be false in any material aspect, with the same punishment as giving false evidence.

ingredients.text: The certificate is required by law to be given or signed, OR the certificate relates to any fact of which such certificate is by law admissible in evidence.

197.punishment: shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.

198.heading: Using as true a certificate known to be false.
198.canonical_text: Prohibits corruptly using or attempting to use a certificate as true, knowing it to be false in any material point.

ingredients.text: The person uses or attempts to use a certificate.
The person uses or attempts to use the certificate as a true certificate.

199.heading: False statement made in declaration which is by law receivable as evidence.
199.canonical_text: A person makes a false statement in a declaration that is legally receivable as evidence, knowing or believing it to be false, or not believing it to be true, concerning a material point.

ingredients.text: Whoever, in any declaration made or subscribed by him
which declaration any Court of Justice, or any public servant or other person, is bound or authorised by law to receive as evidence of any fact
makes any statement which is false
and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true
touching any point material to the object for which the declaration is made or used

199.punishment: punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence

200.heading: Using as true such declaration knowing it to be false.
200.canonical_text: This section criminalizes the corrupt use or attempted use of a declaration as true, knowing it to be false in a material point.

ingredients.text: Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use as true any such declaration
knowing the same to be false in any material point

200.punishment: Punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.

201.heading: Causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information, to screen offender— if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life; if punishable with less than ten Years' imprisonment.
201.canonical_text: A person who, knowing or having reason to believe an offence has been committed, either causes evidence of that offence to disappear or gives false information about it, with the intent to screen the offender from legal punishment.

ingredients.text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed
causes any evidence of the commission of that offence to disappear
gives any information respecting the offence
which he knows or believes to be false
with the intention of screening the offender from legal punishment

201.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

202.heading: Intentional omission to give information of offence by person bound to inform.
202.canonical_text: A person who, knowing or having reason to believe an offence has occurred, intentionally omits to provide legally required information about that offence, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: Whoever knows or has reason to believe that an offence has been committed.
Intentionally omits to give any information respecting that offence.

202.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both

203.heading: Giving false information respecting an offence committed.
203.canonical_text: A person gives information about an offence, knowing or having reason to believe an offence has been committed, and knowing or believing the information to be false.

ingredients.text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed
gives any information respecting that offence
which he knows or believes to be false

203.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

204.heading: Destruction of document to prevent its production as evidence.
204.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who secretes, destroys, obliterates, or renders illegible a document or electronic record that they are lawfully compelled to produce as evidence, with the intent to prevent its production or use in court or before a public servant, or after being summoned to produce it.

ingredients.text: The accused secretes or destroys a document or electronic record.
The accused obliterates or renders illegible the whole or any part of a document or electronic record.
The evidence is for a Court of Justice or any proceeding lawfully held before a public servant.
The accused acts with the intention of preventing the document or electronic record from being produced or used as evidence before such Court or public servant.
The accused acts after having been lawfully summoned or required to produce the document or electronic record for that purpose.

204.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

205.heading: False personation for purpose of act or proceeding in suit or prosecution.
205.canonical_text: Whoever falsely personates another and, in that assumed character, performs certain actions in a legal suit or criminal prosecution, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: That person, in such assumed character, makes any admission or statement.
That person, in such assumed character, does any other act in any suit or criminal prosecution.

205.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both

206.heading: Fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution.
206.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who fraudulently removes, conceals, transfers, or delivers property or an interest therein, with the intent to prevent its seizure as a forfeiture, in satisfaction of a fine under a pronounced or likely sentence, or in execution of a made or likely decree or order by a Court of Justice.

ingredients.text: Whoever fraudulently removes, conceals, transfers or delivers to any person any property or any interest therein
intending thereby to prevent that property or interest therein from being taken as a forfeiture or in satisfaction of a fine
under a sentence which has been pronounced, or which he knows to be likely to be pronounced, by a Court of Justice or other competent authority
or from being taken in execution of a decree or order which has been made, or which he knows to be likely to be made by a Court of Justice in a civil suit

206.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years or with fine, or with both

207.heading: Fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution.
207.canonical_text: Whoever fraudulently accepts, receives, or claims property or an interest in it, knowing they have no right, or practices deception regarding property rights, intending to prevent its seizure as forfeiture, fine satisfaction, or execution of a court order, commits an offense.

ingredients.text: Whoever fraudulently accepts, receives or claims any property or any interest therein
knowing that he has no right or rightful claim to such property or interest
or practices any deception touching any right to any property or any interest therein
intending thereby to prevent that property or interest therein from being taken as a forfeiture or in satisfaction of a fine
under a sentence which has been pronounced, or which he knows to be likely to be pronounced by a Court of Justice or other competent authority
or from being taken in execution of a decree or order which has been made, or which he knows to be likely to be made by a Court of Justice in a civil suit

207.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

208.heading: Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due.
208.canonical_text: Whoever fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be passed against them at the suit of any person for a sum not due, or for a larger sum than is due, or for property to which the person is not entitled, or fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be executed against them after it has been satisfied, or for anything in respect of which it has been satisfied, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: The person causes or suffers a decree or order to be passed against them.
The decree or order is passed at the suit of any person.
The decree or order is for a sum not due.
The decree or order is for a larger sum than is due to such person.
The decree or order is for any property or interest in property to which such person is not entitled.
The person causes or suffers a decree or order to be executed against them.
The execution is for anything in respect of which the decree or order has been satisfied.

208.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

209.heading: Dishonestly making false claim in Court.
209.canonical_text: Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly, or with intent to injure or annoy any person, makes in a Court of Justice any claim which he knows to be false, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: Whoever fraudulently
or dishonestly
or with intent to injure any person
or with intent to annoy any person
makes in a Court of Justice
any claim
which he knows to be false

209.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine

210.heading: Fraudulently obtaining decree for sum not due.
210.canonical_text: This section penalizes individuals who fraudulently obtain decrees or orders for sums or property not due, or for larger amounts than due, or who fraudulently execute satisfied decrees, or permit such acts in their name.

ingredients.text: Whoever fraudulently obtains a decree or order against any person for a sum not due
Whoever fraudulently obtains a decree or order against any person for a larger sum than is due
Whoever fraudulently obtains a decree or order against any person for any property or interest in property to which he is not entitled
Whoever fraudulently causes a decree or order to be executed against any person after it has been satisfied
Whoever fraudulently causes a decree or order to be executed against any person for anything in respect of which it has been satisfied
Whoever fraudulently suffers or permits any such act to be done in his name

210.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

211.heading: False charge of offence made with intent to injure.
211.canonical_text: Whoever, with intent to cause injury to any person, institutes or causes to be instituted any criminal proceeding against that person, or falsely charges any person with having committed an offence, knowing that there is no just or lawful ground for such proceeding or charge against that person.

ingredients.text: Whoever, with intent to cause injury to any person
institutes or causes to be instituted any criminal proceeding against that person, or falsely charges any person with having committed an offence
knowing that there is no just or lawful ground for such proceeding or charge against that person

211.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

212.heading: Harbouring offender.— if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment.
212.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of harbouring or concealing an offender with the intent to screen them from legal punishment, specifying varying punishments based on the severity of the original offence, and includes a definition of 'offence' for acts committed outside India, with an exception for spouses.

ingredients.text: An offence has been committed.
Whoever harbours or conceals a person.
Whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the offender.
With the intention of screening him from legal punishment.

The term 'offence' in this section includes any act committed at any place out of India, which, if committed in India, would be punishable under specific sections (302, 304, 382, 392, 393, 394, 395, 396, 397, 398, 399, 402, 435, 436, 449, 450, 457, 458, 459 and 460).
This provision shall not extend to any case in which the harbour or concealment is by the husband or wife of the offender.

212.punishment: Punishment varies based on the severity of the original offence: up to five years imprisonment and fine for capital offences; up to three years imprisonment and fine for life imprisonment or up to ten years; and up to one-fourth of the original term or fine or both for lesser imprisonable offences.

213.heading: Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment.— if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment.
213.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who accepts or attempts to obtain gratification or restitution of property in exchange for concealing an offence, screening an offender from legal punishment, or not prosecuting an offender, with varying punishments depending on the severity of the original offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever accepts or attempts to obtain, or agrees to accept, any gratification for himself or any other person, or any restitution of property to himself or any other person

in consideration of his concealing an offence or of his screening any person from legal punishment for any offence, or of his not proceeding against any person for the purpose of bringing him to legal punishment
if the offence is punishable with death
if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years
if the offence is punishable with imprisonment not extending to ten years

213.punishment: If the original offence is punishable with death: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and fine. If the original offence is punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and fine. If the original offence is punishable with imprisonment not extending to ten years: imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.

214.heading: Offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender - if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment.
214.canonical_text: This section prohibits offering gratification or restoring property in exchange for concealing an offence, screening an offender from legal punishment, or preventing prosecution, with punishments varying based on the severity of the original offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever gives or causes, or offers or agrees to give or cause, any gratification to any person
Whoever restores or causes the restoration of any property to any person
in consideration of that person's concealing an offence
in consideration of that person's screening any person from legal punishment for any offence
in consideration of that person's not proceeding against any person for the purpose of bringing him to legal punishment

214.punishment: Varies based on the severity of the original offence: up to 7 years imprisonment and fine for capital offences; up to 3 years imprisonment and fine for offences punishable with life imprisonment or up to 10 years; up to one-fourth of the longest term of imprisonment for the original offence, or fine, or both, for lesser offences.

215.heading: Taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc.
215.canonical_text: This section criminalizes anyone who takes or agrees to take gratification under the pretense of helping to recover movable property that was lost due to an offense punishable under this Code, unless they actively work to apprehend and convict the original offender. The punishment includes imprisonment, fine, or both.

ingredients.text: Whoever takes or agrees or consents to take any gratification.
The gratification is taken under pretence or on account of helping any person to recover any movable property.
The movable property was deprived by any offence punishable under this Code.

215.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

216.heading: Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody of whose apprehension has been ordered- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment.
216.canonical_text: This section criminalizes harbouring or concealing a person who has escaped lawful custody or for whom an apprehension order has been issued, with the intent to prevent their apprehension. It outlines different punishments based on the severity of the original offence and provides an exception for spouses.

ingredients.text: The person was convicted of or charged with an offence.
The accused knows of such escape or order for apprehension.
The accused harbours or conceals that person.
The accused acts with the intention of preventing the person from being apprehended.
The provision does not extend to the case in which the harbour or concealment is by the husband or wife of the person to be apprehended.

“Offence” in this section includes any act or omission committed outside India which, if committed in India, would be punishable as an offence, and for which the person is liable to be apprehended or detained under any law relating to extradition or otherwise.

216.punishment: If the original offence is punishable with death: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and fine. If the original offence is punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for ten years: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, with or without fine. If the original offence is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to one year and not to ten years: imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of the imprisonment provided for such offence, or with fine, or with both.

216A.heading: Penalty for harbouring robbers or dacoits.
216A.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who, knowing or believing persons are about to commit or have committed robbery or dacoity, harbors them with the intent to facilitate the crime or screen them from punishment. The location of the robbery/dacoity (within or outside India) is irrelevant, but the provision does not apply if the harbourer is the offender's spouse.

ingredients.text: Whoever knows or has reason to believe that any persons are about to commit robbery or dacoity.
Whoever knows or has reason to believe that any persons have recently committed robbery or dacoity.
Harbours such persons or any of them.
With the intention of facilitating the commission of such robbery or dacoity.
With the intention of screening such persons or any of them from punishment.
It is immaterial whether the robbery or dacoity is intended to be committed, or has been committed, within or without India.
The provision does not apply if the harbour is by the husband or wife of the offender.

216A.punishment: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

216B.heading: [Repealed.]
216B.canonical_text: Section 216B, which defined 'harbour' for sections 212, 216, and 216A, was repealed by the Indian Penal Code (Amendment) Act, 1942 (8 of 1942), s. 3.

ingredients.text: The repeal was by the Indian Penal Code (Amendment) Act, 1942 (8 of 1942).
The repeal was by section 3 of the Indian Penal Code (Amendment) Act, 1942.

status.note: Rep. by the Indian Penal Code (Amendment) Act, 1942 (8 of 1942), s. 3.

217.heading: Public servant disobeying direction of law with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture.
217.canonical_text: A public servant commits an offence if they knowingly disobey a legal direction regarding their conduct, with the intent or knowledge that it will save a person from legal punishment, subject a person to a lesser punishment, or save property from forfeiture or charge.

ingredients.text: The offender knowingly disobeys any direction of the law as to the way in which he is to conduct himself as such public servant.
The offender intends to save any person from legal punishment, or knows it to be likely that he will thereby save any person from legal punishment.

The offender intends to subject any person to a less punishment than that to which he is liable, or knows it to be likely that he will thereby subject any person to a less punishment than that to which he is liable.

The offender intends to save any property from forfeiture or any charge to which it is liable by law, or knows that he is likely thereby to save any property from forfeiture or any charge to which it is liable by law.

217.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

218.heading: Public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture.
218.canonical_text: A public servant charged with preparing a record or writing, who knowingly frames it incorrectly with intent to cause loss or injury, or to save a person from legal punishment, or to save property from forfeiture, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: The public servant is charged with the preparation of any record or other writing.
The public servant frames that record or writing in a manner which he knows to be incorrect.
The public servant acts with intent to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, loss or injury to the public or to any person.
The public servant acts with intent thereby to save, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby save, any person from legal punishment.
The public servant acts with intent to save, or knowing that he is likely thereby to save, any property from forfeiture or other charge to which it is liable by law.

218.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

219.heading: Public servant in judicial proceeding corruptly making report, etc., contrary to law.
219.canonical_text: A public servant who corruptly or maliciously makes or pronounces a report, order, verdict, or decision in a judicial proceeding, knowing it to be contrary to law, commits an offence.
219.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both

220.heading: Commitment for trial or confinement by person having authority who knows that he is acting contrary to law.
220.canonical_text: A person in authority who corruptly or maliciously commits or keeps someone in confinement, knowing it is contrary to law, commits an offense.

ingredients.text: The offender is in an office which gives legal authority to commit persons for trial or to confinement.
The offender is in an office which gives legal authority to keep persons in confinement.
The offender commits any person for trial or to confinement.
The offender keeps any person in confinement.

220.punishment: imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both

221.heading: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend.
221.canonical_text: A public servant, legally bound to apprehend or confine a person charged with or liable for an offence, commits an offence if they intentionally omit to apprehend, suffer escape, or aid in the escape of that person, with varying punishments depending on the severity of the original offence.

ingredients.text: The public servant is legally bound to apprehend or to keep in confinement any person.
The person is charged with or liable to be apprehended for an offence.
The public servant intentionally omits to apprehend such person.
The public servant intentionally suffers such person to escape.
The public servant intentionally aids such person in escaping or attempting to escape from such confinement.

221.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, with or without fine, if the original offence was punishable with death; or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, with or without fine, if the original offence was punishable with imprisonment for life or for a term which may extend to ten years; or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, with or without fine, if the original offence was punishable with imprisonment for a term less than ten years.

222.heading: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend person under sentence or lawfully committed.
222.canonical_text: A public servant, legally bound to apprehend or confine a person under sentence or lawfully committed, intentionally omits to apprehend, or intentionally suffers or aids their escape.

ingredients.text: Whoever, being a public servant
legally bound as such public servant to apprehend or to keep in confinement any person
any person under sentence of a Court of Justice for any offence or lawfully committed to custody
intentionally omits to apprehend such person
intentionally suffers such person to escape
intentionally aids such person in escaping or attempting to escape from such confinement

222.punishment: Punishment varies: imprisonment for life or up to 14 years with or without fine if the person is under sentence of death; up to 7 years with or without fine if the person is under sentence of life imprisonment or 10 years or upwards; up to 3 years, or fine, or both, if the person is under sentence for less than 10 years or lawfully committed to custody.

223.heading: Escape from confinement or custody negligently suffered by public servant.
223.canonical_text: A public servant, legally bound to keep a person in confinement or custody, who negligently allows that person to escape, commits an offence.

ingredients.text: The public servant is legally bound to keep a person in confinement or custody.

normalized.custody_status: charged with offence, convicted of offence, or lawfully committed to custody

ingredients.text: The public servant negligently suffers such person to escape from confinement.

223.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

224.heading: Resistance or obstruction by a person to his lawful apprehension.
224.canonical_text: A person commits an offense if they intentionally resist or obstruct their lawful apprehension for a charged or convicted offense, or escape or attempt to escape from lawful custody for such an offense.

ingredients.text: Whoever intentionally offers any resistance or illegal obstruction
to the lawful apprehension of himself
for any offence with which he is charged or of which he has been convicted
or escapes or attempts to escape
from any custody in which he is lawfully detained
for any such offence

224.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

225.heading: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person.
225.canonical_text: Prohibits intentionally resisting or obstructing lawful apprehension, or rescuing a lawfully detained person, for an offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever intentionally offers any resistance or illegal obstruction.
The resistance or obstruction is to the lawful apprehension of any other person.
The apprehension is for an offence.
Whoever rescues or attempts to rescue any other person.
The other person is from any custody in which that person is lawfully detained.

225.punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both; with higher penalties depending on the severity of the underlying offense.

225A.heading: Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise, provided for.
225A.canonical_text: This section defines the offence committed by a public servant who, being legally bound to apprehend or confine a person, omits to apprehend or suffers the person to escape, in cases not otherwise provided for by specific sections or laws.

ingredients.text: Whoever, being a public servant
legally bound as such public servant to apprehend, or to keep in confinement, any person
in any case not provided for in section 221, section 222 or section 223, or in any other law for the time being in force
omits to apprehend that person
suffers him to escape from confinement

225A.punishment: If done intentionally: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine or with both. If done negligently: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

225B.heading: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension, or escape or rescue in cases not otherwise provided for.
225B.canonical_text: This section penalizes individuals who, in cases not covered by specific other laws, intentionally resist or obstruct lawful apprehension, or escape/attempt to escape from lawful custody, or rescue/attempt to rescue another from lawful custody.

ingredients.text: The case is not provided for in section 224 or section 225 or in any other law for the time being in force.
Whoever intentionally offers any resistance or illegal obstruction to the lawful apprehension of himself or of any other person.
Whoever escapes or attempts to escape from any custody in which he is lawfully detained.
Whoever rescues or attempts to rescue any other person from any custody in which that person is lawfully detained.

225B.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both

226.heading: [Repealed.]
226.canonical_text: This section, which previously addressed unlawful return from transportation, has been repealed by the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1955.

status.note: Repealed by the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1955 (26 of 1955), s. 117 and the Sch (w.e.f. 1-1-1956).

227.heading: Violation of condition of remission of punishment.
227.canonical_text: Whoever, having accepted a conditional remission of punishment, knowingly violates any condition on which such remission was granted, shall be punished with the original sentence or the unserved portion thereof.

ingredients.text: Whoever, having accepted any conditional remission of punishment
knowingly violates any condition on which such remission was granted

227.punishment: The punishment to which he was originally sentenced, or if he has suffered any part of that punishment, then so much of that punishment as he has not already suffered.

228.heading: Intentional insult or interruption to public servant sitting in judicial proceeding.
228.canonical_text: Whoever intentionally insults or interrupts a public servant during a judicial proceeding shall be punished with imprisonment, fine, or both.

ingredients.text: Whoever intentionally offers any insult
or causes any interruption to any public servant
while such public servant is sitting in any stage of a judicial proceeding

normalized.context: public servant sitting in judicial proceeding

228.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both

228A.heading: Disclosure of identity of the victim of certain offences, etc.
228A.canonical_text: This section prohibits the printing or publication of the identity of victims of certain sexual offenses (sections 376, 376A, 376AB, 376B, 376C, 376D, 376DA, 376E), punishable with imprisonment up to two years and fine. Exceptions apply if done under police order for investigation, with victim's written authorization, or with next of kin's authorization (for dead, minor, or unsound mind victims) to a recognized welfare institution. It also prohibits publishing court proceedings related to these offenses without court permission, with an exception for High Court or Supreme Court judgments.

ingredients.text: A person prints or publishes.
The published content is the name or any matter which may make known the identity of a person.

The person whose identity is revealed is a victim against whom an offence under section 376, section 376A, section 376AB, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA or section 376E is alleged or found to have been committed.

The printing or publication is by or under the order in writing of the officer-in-charge of the police station or the police officer making the investigation into such offence, acting in good faith for the purposes of such investigation.
The printing or publication is by, or with the authorisation in writing of, the victim.
Where the victim is dead or minor or of unsound mind, the printing or publication is by, or with the authorisation in writing of, the next of kin of the victim.
Such authorisation by the next of kin is given only to the chairman or the secretary of any recognised welfare institution or organisation.
A 'recognised welfare institution or organisation' means a social welfare institution or organization recognised in this behalf by the Central or State Government.
A person prints or publishes any matter in relation to any proceeding before a court.
The proceeding relates to an offence referred to in sub-section (1).
The printing or publication of the judgment of any High Court or the Supreme Court does not amount to an offence within the meaning of this section.

228A.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years and shall also be liable to fine

229.heading: Personation of a juror or assessor.
229.canonical_text: This section defines the offense of personation of a juror or assessor, where an individual intentionally causes or knowingly allows themselves to be returned, empanelled, or sworn as a juror or assessor despite knowing they are not legally entitled, or voluntarily serves after being unlawfully returned, empanelled, or sworn.

ingredients.text: Whoever, by personation or otherwise, shall intentionally cause, or knowingly suffer himself to be returned, empanelled or sworn as a juryman or assessor.
in any case in which he knows that he is not entitled by law to be so returned, empanelled or sworn.
or knowing himself to have been so returned, empanelled or sworn contrary to law, shall voluntarily serve on such jury or as such assessor.

229.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

229A.heading: Failure by person released on bail or bond to appear in Court.
229A.canonical_text: A person charged with an offence and released on bail or bond without sureties, who fails without sufficient cause to appear in court as per the terms of the bail or bond, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: Whoever, having been charged with an offence
and released on bail or on bond without sureties
fails without sufficient cause (the burden of proving which shall lie upon him)
to appear in court in accordance with the terms of the bail or bond

229A.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both

230.heading: “Coin” defined.
230.canonical_text: This section defines 'Coin' as metal used as money, stamped and issued by a State or Sovereign Power. It also defines 'Indian coin' as metal stamped and issued by the Government of India for use as money, retaining this status even if no longer used as money.

ingredients.text: Coin is metal used for the time being as money, and stamped and issued by the authority of some State or Sovereign Power in order to be so used.
Indian coin is metal stamped and issued by the authority of the Government of India in order to be used as money
metal which has been so stamped and issued shall continue to be Indian coin for the purposes of this Chapter, notwithstanding that it may have ceased to be used as money.

normalized.condition: ceased to be used as money

231.heading: Counterfeiting coin.
231.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of counterfeiting coin, which includes both direct counterfeiting and knowingly participating in the counterfeiting process. It also clarifies that altering a genuine coin with intent to deceive, or knowing that deception is likely, to make it appear as a different coin constitutes this offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever counterfeits coin
Whoever knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting coin
A person commits this offence who intending to practise deception
A person commits this offence who knowing it to be likely that deception will thereby be practised
causes a genuine coin to appear like a different coin

231.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

232.heading: Counterfeiting Indian coin.
232.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of counterfeiting Indian coin and prescribes the punishment for it.

ingredients.text: Whoever counterfeits
or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting

232.punishment: imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

233.heading: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting coin.
233.canonical_text: This section prohibits making, mending, buying, selling, or disposing of any die or instrument intended for counterfeiting coin, or with knowledge or reason to believe it is intended for such use.

ingredients.text: Whoever makes or mends, or performs any part of the process of making or mending

normalized.action: makes, mends, performs part of process

ingredients.text: or buys, sells or disposes of
any die or instrument
for the purpose of being used for the purpose of counterfeiting coin

normalized.intent: to be used for counterfeiting coin

ingredients.text: or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used for the purpose of counterfeiting coin

233.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extended to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

234.heading: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting Indian coin.
234.canonical_text: This section prohibits making, mending, processing, buying, selling, or disposing of any die or instrument with the intent or knowledge that it will be used for counterfeiting Indian coin.

ingredients.text: Whoever makes or mends
or performs any part of the process of making or mending
or buys, sells or disposes of
any die or instrument
for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for the purpose of counterfeiting 1[Indian coin]

234.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

235.heading: Possession of instrument or material for the purpose of using the same for counterfeiting coin: if Indian coin.
235.canonical_text: This section criminalizes the possession of any instrument or material intended for counterfeiting coins, with a higher penalty if the coin to be counterfeited is Indian coin.

ingredients.text: Whoever is in possession of any instrument or material
for the purpose of using the same for counterfeiting coin
or knowing or having reason to believe that the same is intended to be used for that purpose
the coin to be counterfeited is Indian coin

235.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

236.heading: Abetting in India the counterfeiting out of India of coin.
236.canonical_text: This section punishes a person who, while in India, abets the counterfeiting of coin that takes place outside India, treating it as if the abetment occurred within India for punishment purposes.

ingredients.text: The person abets the counterfeiting of coin.

237.heading: Import or export of counterfeit coin.
237.canonical_text: This section prohibits the import or export of counterfeit coin by anyone who knows or has reason to believe it is counterfeit, and prescribes punishment for such acts.

ingredients.text: Whoever imports into India
or exports therefrom
any counterfeit coin
knowing or having reason to believe that the same is counterfeit

237.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

238.heading: Import or export of counterfeits of the Indian coin.
238.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who imports into or exports from India any counterfeit Indian coin, knowing or having reason to believe it to be counterfeit.

ingredients.text: Whoever imports into India
or exports therefrom
any counterfeit coin
which he knows or has reason to believe to be a counterfeit of Indian coin

238.punishment: Imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

239.heading: Delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit.
239.canonical_text: This section penalizes the delivery or attempted delivery of counterfeit coin by a person who knew it was counterfeit when they acquired it, with fraudulent intent.

ingredients.text: The accused delivers the counterfeit coin to any person.
The accused attempts to induce any person to receive the counterfeit coin.

239.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine

240.heading: Delivery of Indian coin, possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit.
240.canonical_text: This section criminalizes the act of delivering or attempting to induce someone to receive a counterfeit Indian coin, knowing it to be counterfeit at the time of possession, with fraudulent intent.

ingredients.text: The coin is a counterfeit of Indian coin.
The accused delivers the coin to any person.
The accused attempts to induce any person to receive the coin.

240.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

241.heading: Delivery of coin as genuine, which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be counterfeit.
241.canonical_text: This section punishes anyone who delivers or attempts to induce another to receive as genuine any counterfeit coin, knowing it to be counterfeit at the time of delivery, but not knowing it to be counterfeit when first possessed.

ingredients.text: Whoever delivers to any other person as genuine, or attempts to induce any other person to receive as genuine, any counterfeit coin.
The person knows the coin to be counterfeit at the time of delivery.
The person did not know the coin to be counterfeit at the time when they took it into their possession.

241.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine to an amount which may extend to ten times the value of the coin counterfeited, or with both.

242.heading: Possession of counterfeit coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof.
242.canonical_text: A person who fraudulently or with intent to commit fraud possesses counterfeit coin, knowing it to be counterfeit at the time of possession, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: Whoever
fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed
is in possession of counterfeit coin
having known at the time when he became possessed thereof that such coin was counterfeit

242.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine

243.heading: Possession of Indian coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof.
243.canonical_text: This section penalizes the fraudulent possession of counterfeit Indian coin by a person who knew it was counterfeit at the time of acquiring it.

ingredients.text: The person acts fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed.
The person is in possession of a coin.
The coin is counterfeit.
The coin is a counterfeit of Indian coin.

243.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

244.heading: Person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law.
244.canonical_text: Any person employed in a lawfully established mint in India who intentionally acts or omits to act, causing a coin issued from that mint to have a different weight or composition than legally fixed, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: Whoever, being employed in any mint lawfully established in India
does any act, or omits what he is legally bound to do
with the intention of causing any coin issued from that mint to be of a different weight or composition from the weight or composition fixed by law

244.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

245.heading: Unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint.
245.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who, without lawful authority, removes a coining tool or instrument from any lawfully established mint in India.

ingredients.text: Takes out of any mint.

245.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

246.heading: Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of coin.
246.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who fraudulently or dishonestly performs an operation on a coin that either diminishes its weight or alters its composition. An explanation clarifies that scooping out part of a coin and inserting other material constitutes altering its composition.

ingredients.text: The operation diminishes the weight of that coin.
The operation alters the composition of that coin.
Scooping out part of the coin and putting anything else into the cavity alters the composition of the coin.

246.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

247.heading: Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of Indian coin.
247.canonical_text: Performing an operation on an Indian coin that fraudulently or dishonestly diminishes its weight or alters its composition.

ingredients.text: The operation diminishes the weight of the coin.
The operation alters the composition of the coin.

247.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

248.heading: Altering appearance of coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description.
248.canonical_text: Performing an operation on a coin to alter its appearance with the intent that it passes as a coin of a different description.

ingredients.text: Whoever performs on any coin any operation which alters the appearance of that coin
with the intention that the said coin shall pass as a coin of a different description

248.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

249.heading: Altering appearance of Indian coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description.
249.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who alters the appearance of an Indian coin with the intent that it passes as a coin of a different description.

ingredients.text: Whoever performs on any Indian coin any operation which alters the appearance of that coin
with the intention that the said coin shall pass as a coin of a different description

249.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

250.heading: Delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered.
250.canonical_text: This section criminalizes the act of delivering or attempting to induce another to receive coin, knowing it to be altered as per sections 246 or 248, with fraudulent intent.

ingredients.text: An offence defined in section 246 or 248 has been committed with respect to the coin.
The accused acts fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed.
The accused delivers such coin to any other person.
The accused attempts to induce any other person to receive the same coin.

250.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

251.heading: Delivery of Indian coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered.
251.canonical_text: This section defines the offense of delivering or attempting to induce another to receive Indian coin, knowing it to be altered as per sections 247 or 249, with fraudulent intent.

ingredients.text: The person has coin in their possession.
An offence defined in section 247 or 249 has been committed with respect to that coin.
The person knew, at the time of possession, that such an offence had been committed with respect to the coin.
The person acts fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed.
The person delivers such coin to any other person.
The person attempts to induce any other person to receive the same.

251.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

252.heading: Possession of coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof.
252.canonical_text: Possession of coin known to be altered, with fraudulent intent, where an offence under section 246 or 248 has been committed.

ingredients.text: Whoever is in possession of coin.
The possession is fraudulent or with intent that fraud may be committed.
An offence defined in either of section 246 or 248 has been committed with respect to the coin.
The person knew at the time of becoming possessed thereof that such offence had been committed with respect to such coin.

252.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

253.heading: Possession of Indian coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof.
253.canonical_text: A person is in possession of a coin, knowing it to be altered (as per sections 247 or 249), with fraudulent intent.

ingredients.text: Whoever is in possession of coin
The possession is fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed
The coin is one with respect to which the offence defined in either of the section 247 or 249 has been committed
The person knew at the time of becoming possessed thereof, that such offence had been committed with respect to such coin

253.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

254.heading: Delivery of coin as genuine which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be altered.
254.canonical_text: Whoever delivers or attempts to induce another to receive as genuine an altered coin, knowing it to be altered at the time of delivery but not at the time of initial possession.

ingredients.text: Whoever delivers to any other person as genuine or as a coin of a different description from what it is
or attempts to induce any person to receive as genuine, or as a different coin from what it is
any coin in respect of which he knows that any such operation as that mentioned in sections 246, 247, 248 or 249 has been performed
but in respect of which he did not, at the time when he took it into his possession, know that such operation had been performed

254.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine to an amount which may extend to ten times the value of the coin for which the altered coin is passed, or attempted to be passed.

255.heading: Counterfeiting Government stamp.
255.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who counterfeits or knowingly participates in the counterfeiting process of any government-issued revenue stamp. An explanation clarifies that causing a genuine stamp of one denomination to appear as another constitutes this offense.

ingredients.text: Whoever counterfeits
or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting
any stamp issued by Government
for the purpose of revenue
A person commits this offence who counterfeits by causing a genuine stamps of one denomination to appear like a genuine stamp of a different denomination.

255.punishment: imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

256.heading: Having possession of instrument or material for counterfeiting Government stamp.
256.canonical_text: This section penalizes the possession of any instrument or material intended or known to be intended for counterfeiting government revenue stamps.

ingredients.text: Whoever has in his possession any instrument or material.
The instrument or material is for the purpose of being used for counterfeiting any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue.
The person knows or has reason to believe that the instrument or material is intended to be used for counterfeiting any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue.

256.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

257.heading: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting Government stamp.
257.canonical_text: This section criminalizes the making, buying, selling, or disposing of any instrument intended for or known to be intended for counterfeiting government revenue stamps.

ingredients.text: The instrument is for the purpose of being used for counterfeiting any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue.
The accused knows or has reason to believe that the instrument is intended to be used for the purpose of counterfeiting any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue.

257.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

258.heading: Sale of counterfeit Government stamp.
258.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who sells or offers for sale a stamp known or believed to be a counterfeit of a government revenue stamp.

ingredients.text: Whoever sells, or offers for sale
any stamp
which he knows or has reason to believe
to be a counterfeit of any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue

258.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

259.heading: Having possession of counterfeit Government stamp.
259.canonical_text: This section criminalizes the possession of a counterfeit government revenue stamp with the knowledge that it is counterfeit and with the intent to use or dispose of it as genuine.

ingredients.text: The person knows the stamp to be a counterfeit.

299.heading: Culpable homicide.
299.canonical_text: Defines culpable homicide as causing death with the intention of causing death, or causing bodily injury likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that the act is likely to cause death. A person who causes bodily injury to another who is labouring under a disorder, disease or bodily infirmity, and thereby accelerates the death of that other, shall be deemed to have caused his death.

Where death is caused by bodily injury, the person who causes such bodily injury shall be deemed to have caused the death, although by resorting to proper remedies and skilful treatment the death might have been prevented.
The causing of the death of a child in the mother's womb is not homicide.
It may amount to culpable homicide to cause the death of a living child, if any part of that child has been brought forth, though the child may not have breathed or been completely born.
