304A.canonical_text: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: Whoever causes the death of any person
by doing any rash or negligent act
not amounting to culpable homicide

304A.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

status.note: Marked as omitted/repealed in source text.

304B.heading: Dowry death.
304B.canonical_text: Defines 'dowry death' as the death of a woman within seven years of marriage due to burns, bodily injury, or abnormal circumstances, where she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relatives for dowry demand, and prescribes punishment for committing such an offence.

ingredients.text: the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury
the death of a woman occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances
the death occurs within seven years of her marriage
soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment
cruelty or harassment by her husband
cruelty or harassment by any relative of her husband
cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry
dowry shall have the same meaning as in section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (28 of 1961)

304B.punishment: imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life

305.heading: Abetment of suicide of child or insane person.
305.canonical_text: This section defines the punishment for abetting the suicide of a person who is under eighteen years of age, insane, delirious, an idiot, or in a state of intoxication.

ingredients.text: A person commits suicide.
Whoever abets the commission of such suicide.

305.punishment: death or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

306.heading: Abetment of suicide.
306.canonical_text: Whoever abets the commission of suicide, where any person commits suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment and fine.

ingredients.text: any person commits suicide
whoever abets the commission of such suicide

306.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

307.heading: Attempt to murder.
307.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of attempt to murder as performing an act with the intention or knowledge that if it caused death, the perpetrator would be guilty of murder. It prescribes punishment for such attempts, with enhanced penalties if hurt is caused, including for life-convicts.

ingredients.text: Whoever does any act
with such intention or knowledge
and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder
if hurt is caused to any person by such act
When any person offending under this section is under sentence of imprisonment for life
if hurt is caused (by a life-convict)

307.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned; and when any person offending under this section is under sentence of imprisonment for life, he may, if hurt is caused, be punished with death.

308.heading: Attempt to commit culpable homicide.
308.canonical_text: Whoever does any act with the intention or knowledge and under circumstances that if death were caused, it would be culpable homicide not amounting to murder, commits an offence. If hurt is caused by such act, the punishment is enhanced.

ingredients.text: Whoever does any act
with such intention or knowledge
and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder
if hurt is caused to any person by such act

308.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if hurt is caused, imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

309.heading: Attempt to commit suicide.
309.canonical_text: This section criminalizes the attempt to commit suicide, requiring an overt act towards the commission of the offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever attempts to commit suicide
and does any act towards the commission of such offence

309.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine, or with both

310.heading: Thug.
310.canonical_text: This section defines a 'thug' as someone habitually associated with others for the purpose of committing robbery or child-stealing by means of or accompanied with murder, at any time after the passing of this Act.

ingredients.text: The person must have been habitually associated with any other or others at any time after the passing of this Act.
The robbery or child-stealing must be by means of or accompanied with murder.

311.heading: Punishment.
311.canonical_text: Punishment for being a thug includes imprisonment for life and a fine.

312.heading: Causing miscarriage.
312.canonical_text: Voluntarily causing a woman with child to miscarry, unless done in good faith to save her life, is an offense. If the woman is quick with child, the punishment is more severe. A woman causing her own miscarriage is included within the meaning of this section.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry
such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman
the woman be quick with child
A woman who causes herself to miscarry, is within the meaning of this section

312.punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years and fine

313.heading: Causing miscarriage without woman's consent.
313.canonical_text: This section defines the punishment for causing miscarriage without the woman's consent, irrespective of whether she is quick with child.

ingredients.text: Whoever commits the offence defined in the last preceding section
without the consent of the woman
whether the woman is quick with child or not

313.punishment: imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

314.heading: Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage.
314.canonical_text: Whoever, with intent to cause the miscarriage of a woman with child, does any act which causes her death, is punishable. If the act is done without the woman's consent, the punishment is more severe. It is not essential that the offender knows the act is likely to cause death.

ingredients.text: The offender must have the intent to cause the miscarriage of a woman with child.
It is not essential that the offender should know that the act is likely to cause death.
The act is done without the consent of the woman.

314.punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

315.heading: Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause it to die after birth.
315.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of performing an act before a child's birth with the intent to prevent it from being born alive or to cause its death after birth, and actually achieving that outcome, unless the act was done in good faith to save the mother's life.

ingredients.text: A person does any act before the birth of any child.
The act is done with the intention of preventing that child from being born alive.
The act is done with the intention of causing the child to die after its birth.
The act prevents that child from being born alive.
The act causes the child to die after its birth.
The act is not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the mother.

315.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, or with both

316.heading: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide.
316.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of causing the death of a quick unborn child by an act that would amount to culpable homicide if it caused death, and prescribes punishment.

ingredients.text: Whoever does any act under such circumstances, that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide
and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child

316.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

317.heading: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years, by parent or person having care of it.
317.canonical_text: This section penalizes a parent or person having care of a child under twelve years who exposes or leaves the child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning it.

ingredients.text: Whoever being the father or mother of a child under the age of twelve years, or having the care of such child
a child under the age of twelve years
shall expose or leave such child in any place
with the intention of wholly abandoning such child

317.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both

318.heading: Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body.
318.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who intentionally conceals or attempts to conceal the birth of a child by secretly burying or disposing of its dead body, regardless of whether the child died before, during, or after birth.

ingredients.text: secretly burying or otherwise disposing of the dead body of a child
whether such child die before or after or during its birth
intentionally
conceals or endeavors to conceal the birth of such child

318.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

319.heading: Hurt.
319.canonical_text: Defines 'hurt' as causing bodily pain, disease, or infirmity to any person.

ingredients.text: Whoever causes bodily pain
Whoever causes disease
Whoever causes infirmity
to any person

320.heading: Grievous hurt.
320.canonical_text: This section defines the specific types of hurt that are designated as "grievous".

ingredients.text: Emasculation.
Permanent privation of the sight of either eye.
Permanent privation of the hearing of either ear.
Privation of any member or joint.
Destruction or permanent impairing of the powers of any member or joint.
Permanent disfiguration of the head or face.
Fracture or dislocation of a bone or tooth.
Any hurt which endangers life.
Any hurt which causes the sufferer to be during the space of twenty days in severe bodily pain.
Any hurt which causes the sufferer to be during the space of twenty days unable to follow his ordinary pursuits.

321.heading: Voluntarily causing hurt.
321.canonical_text: Defines voluntarily causing hurt as doing an act with the intention or knowledge of causing hurt, and actually causing hurt.

ingredients.text: Whoever does any act
with the intention of thereby causing hurt to any person
or with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause hurt to any person
and does thereby cause hurt to any person

322.heading: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt.
322.canonical_text: This section defines voluntarily causing grievous hurt as when a person voluntarily causes hurt, intending or knowing it is likely to be grievous hurt, and the hurt caused is indeed grievous hurt.

ingredients.text: The accused intends to cause grievous hurt or knows himself to be likely to cause grievous hurt.

323.heading: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt.
323.canonical_text: This section prescribes the punishment for voluntarily causing hurt, with an exception for cases covered by section 334.

ingredients.text: Whoever
except in the case provided for by section 334
voluntarily causes hurt

323.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both

324.heading: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means.
324.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of voluntarily causing hurt using specific dangerous instruments, substances, or animals, with an exception for cases under section 334, and prescribes the associated punishment.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt
except in the case provided for by section 334
by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting
or any instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death

normalized.instrument_characteristic: likely to cause death when used as weapon

ingredients.text: or by means of fire or any heated substance
or by means of any poison or any corrosive substance
or by means of any explosive substance
or by means of any substance which it is deleterious to the human body to inhale, to swallow, or to receive into the blood

normalized.substance_effect: deleterious to human body (inhale, swallow, receive into blood)

ingredients.text: or by means of any animal

324.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both

325.heading: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt.
325.canonical_text: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt, except in cases provided for by section 335, shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years and a fine.

ingredients.text: Whoever
voluntarily causes grievous hurt
except in the case provided for by section 335

325.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

326.heading: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means.
326.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt using dangerous weapons or means, and prescribes the associated punishment.

ingredients.text: The person voluntarily causes grievous hurt.
The grievous hurt is caused by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting.
The grievous hurt is caused by means of any instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death.
The grievous hurt is caused by means of fire or any heated substance.
The grievous hurt is caused by means of any poison or any corrosive substance.
The grievous hurt is caused by means of any explosive substance.
The grievous hurt is caused by means of any substance which it is deleterious to the human body to inhale, to swallow, or to receive into the blood.
The grievous hurt is caused by means of any animal.

326.punishment: imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

326A.heading: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc.
326A.canonical_text: Whoever causes permanent or partial damage, deformity, burns, maiming, disfigurement, or disability to a person's body, or causes grievous hurt, by using acid or other means, with the intent or knowledge of causing such injury.

ingredients.text: Whoever causes permanent or partial damage or deformity to, or burns or maims or disfigures or disables, any part or parts of the body of a person
or causes grievous hurt
by throwing acid on or by administering acid to that person
or by using any other means
with the intention of causing such injury or hurt
or with the knowledge that he is likely to cause such injury or hurt

326A.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and with fine

326B.heading: Voluntarily throwing or attempting to throw acid.
326B.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who throws, attempts to throw, or attempts to administer acid, or attempts to use any other means, with the intention of causing severe harm, disfigurement, or disability. It also defines 'acid' and clarifies the nature of damage.

ingredients.text: The accused throws or attempts to throw acid on any person.
The accused attempts to administer acid to any person.
The accused attempts to use any other means.
The accused acts with the intention of causing permanent or partial damage or deformity or burns or maiming or disfigurement or disability or grievous hurt to that person.

For the purposes of this section, 'acid' includes any substance which has acidic or corrosive character or burning nature, that is capable of causing bodily injury leading to scars or disfigurement or temporary or permanent disability.
For the purposes of this section, permanent or partial damage or deformity shall not be required to be irreversible.

326B.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term not less than five years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

327.heading: Voluntarily causing hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act.
327.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of voluntarily causing hurt with the intent to extort property or valuable security, or to compel the victim or an interested party to commit an illegal act or facilitate an offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt
for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer, or from any person interested in the sufferer, any property or valuable security

normalized.target_of_extortion: sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer

ingredients.text: or of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer to do anything which is illegal

normalized.target_of_constraint: sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer

ingredients.text: or which may facilitate the commission of an offence

normalized.purpose: constraining to do anything which may facilitate the commission of an offence
normalized.target_of_constraint: sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer

327.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

328.heading: Causing hurt by means of poison, etc., with intent to commit an offence.
328.canonical_text: Whoever administers or causes to be taken by any person any poison, stupefying, intoxicating or unwholesome drug, or other thing, with intent to cause hurt, or with intent to commit or facilitate an offence, or knowing it is likely to cause hurt.

ingredients.text: Whoever administers to or causes to be taken by any person
any poison or any stupefying, intoxicating or unwholesome drug, or other thing
with intent to cause hurt to such person
with intent to commit or to facilitate the commission of an offence
knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause hurt

328.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

329.heading: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act.
329.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who voluntarily causes grievous hurt with the purpose of extorting property or valuable security, or to compel the sufferer or an interested person to commit an illegal act or facilitate an offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt
for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer or from any person interested in the sufferer any property or valuable security
for the purpose of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer to do anything that is illegal
for the purpose of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer to do anything which may facilitate the commission of an offence

329.punishment: imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

330.heading: Voluntarily causing hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property.
330.canonical_text: This section criminalizes voluntarily causing hurt with the purpose of extorting a confession or information, or to compel the restoration of property, valuable security, or the satisfaction of a claim or demand.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt
for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer or from any person interested in the sufferer, any confession
for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer or from any person interested in the sufferer, any information which may lead to the detection of an offence or misconduct
for the purpose of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer to restore any property or valuable security
for the purpose of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer to cause the restoration of any property or valuable security
for the purpose of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer to satisfy any claim or demand
for the purpose of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer to give information which may lead to the restoration of any property or valuable security

330.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

331.heading: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property.
331.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt with the intent to extort a confession or information, or to compel the restoration of property, satisfaction of a claim, or provision of information for property restoration.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt
for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer or from any person interested in the sufferer any confession

normalized.target_of_extortion: sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer

ingredients.text: or any information which may lead to the detection of an offence or misconduct

normalized.information_use: detection of an offence or misconduct

ingredients.text: or for the purpose of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer to restore or to cause the restoration of any property or valuable security

normalized.target_of_constraint: sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer

ingredients.text: or to satisfy any claim or demand
or to give information which may lead to the restoration of any property or valuable security

normalized.information_use: restoration of any property or valuable security

331.punishment: Imprisonment up to ten years and fine.

332.heading: Voluntarily causing hurt to deter public servant from his duty.
332.canonical_text: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt to a public servant either while the public servant is discharging their duty, or with the intent to prevent or deter them or any other public servant from discharging their duty, or in consequence of their lawful discharge of duty.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt
to any person being a public servant
the hurt is caused with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty as such public servant
the hurt is caused in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by that person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant

332.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both

status.note: Marked as omitted/repealed in source text.

333.heading: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty.
333.canonical_text: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt to a public servant, either while they are discharging their duty, or with intent to prevent them or another public servant from discharging their duty, or in consequence of their lawful discharge of duty, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and a fine.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt
to any person being a public servant
in the discharge of his duty as such public servant
or with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty as such public servant
or in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by that person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant

333.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

334.heading: Voluntarily causing hurt on provocation.
334.canonical_text: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt on grave and sudden provocation, without intending or knowing to cause hurt to anyone other than the provocateur, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt
The offender neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation

334.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both

335.heading: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt on provocation.
335.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt under grave and sudden provocation, where the offender does not intend or know they are likely to cause grievous hurt to anyone other than the provocateur, and specifies the punishment.

ingredients.text: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt
on grave and sudden provocation
if he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause grievous hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation

normalized.knowledge: not likely to cause grievous hurt

335.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to four years, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both

336.heading: Act endangering life or personal safety of others.
336.canonical_text: Doing any act rashly or negligently that endangers human life or the personal safety of others.

ingredients.text: The act endangers human life or the personal safety of others.

336.punishment: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to two hundred and fifty rupees, or both.

337.heading: Causing hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others.
337.canonical_text: Whoever causes hurt to any person by doing any act rashly or negligently, thereby endangering human life or personal safety, shall be punished with imprisonment, fine, or both.

ingredients.text: Whoever causes hurt to any person
by doing any act so rashly or negligently
as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others

337.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both

338.heading: Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others.
338.canonical_text: Whoever causes grievous hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others.

ingredients.text: Whoever causes grievous hurt to any person
by doing any act
so rashly or negligently
as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others

normalized.endangerment: human life or personal safety of others

338.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

339.heading: Wrongful restraint.
339.canonical_text: Wrongful restraint is committed when a person voluntarily obstructs another, thereby preventing them from proceeding in a direction they have a right to proceed, unless the obstruction is of a private way and the obstructor genuinely believes they have a lawful right to obstruct it.

ingredients.text: A person voluntarily obstructs another person.
The direction is one in which that person has a right to proceed.
Exception: The obstruction is of a private way over land or water.
Exception: The obstructor in good faith believes himself to have a lawful right to obstruct the private way.

340.heading: Wrongful confinement.
340.canonical_text: Wrongful confinement occurs when a person wrongfully restrains another, preventing them from moving beyond specific circumscribing limits.

ingredients.text: The restraint prevents that person from proceeding beyond certain circumscribing limits.

341.heading: Punishment for wrongful restraint.
341.canonical_text: This section prescribes punishment for the act of wrongfully restraining any person.

ingredients.text: A person
wrongfully restrains
any person

341.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both

342.heading: Punishment for wrongful confinement.

ingredients.text: Whoever
wrongfully confines
any person

342.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

343.heading: Wrongful confinement for three or more days.
343.canonical_text: Wrongful confinement of a person for three or more days.

ingredients.text: A person wrongfully confines another person.

343.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

344.heading: Wrongful confinement for ten or more days.
344.canonical_text: This section punishes anyone who wrongfully confines a person for a period of ten days or more, with imprisonment and a fine.

ingredients.text: Whoever wrongfully confines any person
for ten days, or more

344.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

345.heading: Wrongful confinement of person for whose liberation writ has been issued.
345.canonical_text: This section penalizes wrongful confinement of a person by someone who knows that a writ for that person's liberation has been duly issued, with imprisonment up to two years.

ingredients.text: Whoever keeps any person in wrongful confinement
knowing that a writ for the liberation of that person has been duly issued

345.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years in addition to any term of imprisonment to which he may be liable under any other section of this Chapter.

346.heading: Wrongful confinement in secret.
346.canonical_text: This section defines the offense of wrongful confinement in secret, where a person is wrongfully confined with the intent that the confinement or its location remains unknown to interested parties or public servants, and prescribes the punishment for such an act.

ingredients.text: Whoever wrongfully confines any person
in such manner as to indicate an intention that the confinement of such person may not be known to any person interested in the person so confined
or to any public servant
or that the place of such confinement may not be known to or discovered by any such person or public servant as hereinbefore mentioned

346.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years in addition to any other punishment to which he may be liable for such wrongful confinement.

347.heading: Wrongful confinement to extort property, or constrain to illegal act.
347.canonical_text: Wrongful confinement of a person for the purpose of extorting property or valuable security, or to compel an illegal act or to obtain information facilitating an offence.

ingredients.text: Whoever wrongfully confines any person
for the purpose of extorting from the person confined, or from any person interested in the person confined, any property or valuable security
for the purpose of constraining the person confined or any person interested in such person to do anything illegal
for the purpose of constraining the person confined or any person interested in such person to give any information which may facilitate the commission of an offence

347.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine

348.heading: Wrongful confinement to extort confession, or compel restoration of property.
348.canonical_text: Whoever wrongfully confines any person for the purpose of extorting a confession or information about an offence/misconduct, or for compelling the restoration of property/valuable security, or satisfying a claim/demand, or obtaining information leading to property restoration.

ingredients.text: Whoever wrongfully confines any person
for the purpose of extorting from the person confined or any person interested in the person confined any confession
or any information which may lead to the detection of an offence or misconduct
or for the purpose of constraining the person confined or any person interested in the person confined to restore or to cause the restoration of any property or valuable security
or to satisfy any claim or demand
or to give information which may lead to the restoration of any property or valuable security

348.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine

349.heading: Force.
349.canonical_text: This section defines 'force' as causing motion, change of motion, or cessation of motion to another person, or causing a substance to move in a way that contacts the person or their belongings, provided it is done by bodily power, by disposing a substance, or by inducing an animal to move.

ingredients.text: A person causes motion, change of motion, or cessation of motion to another.
A person causes to any substance such motion, or change of motion, or cessation of motion as brings that substance into contact with any part of that other's body.
A person causes to any substance such motion, or change of motion, or cessation of motion as brings that substance into contact with anything which that other is wearing or carrying.

A person causes to any substance such motion, or change of motion, or cessation of motion as brings that substance into contact with anything so situated that such contact affects that other's sense of feeling.
The person causing the motion, or change of motion, or cessation of motion, causes that motion, change of motion, or cessation of motion by his own bodily power.

The person causing the motion, or change of motion, or cessation of motion, causes that motion, change of motion, or cessation of motion by disposing any substance in such a manner that the motion or change or cessation of motion takes place without any further act on his part, or on the part of any other person.

350.heading: Criminal force.
350.canonical_text: Whoever intentionally uses force to any person without that person's consent, either to commit an offence or with the intent or knowledge that such force is likely to cause injury, fear, or annoyance, is said to use criminal force.

ingredients.text: Whoever intentionally uses force to any person
without that person's consent
in order to the committing of any offence

351.heading: Assault.
351.canonical_text: Defines assault as making a gesture or preparation with the intent or knowledge that it will cause a person present to apprehend the imminent use of criminal force.

352.heading: Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation.
352.canonical_text: This section punishes anyone who assaults or uses criminal force against another person, unless it is due to grave and sudden provocation from that person. The punishment can be imprisonment up to three months, a fine up to five hundred rupees, or both. The explanation clarifies conditions under which provocation will not mitigate the punishment, such as if it was sought by the offender, given in obedience to law, or in lawful exercise of private defence.

ingredients.text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person
otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person
if the provocation is sought or voluntarily provoked by the offender as an excuse for the offence
if the provocation is given by anything done in obedience to the law, or by a public servant, in the lawful exercise of the powers of such public servant
if the provocation is given by anything done in the lawful exercise of the right of private defence

352.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

353.heading: Assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty.
353.canonical_text: This section defines the offense of assaulting or using criminal force against a public servant to deter them from their duty or in consequence of their official actions.

with intent to prevent or deter that person from discharging his duty as such public servant
in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by such person to the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant

353.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

354A.heading: Sexual harassment and punishment for sexual harassment.
354A.canonical_text: This section defines sexual harassment as a man committing specific acts including unwelcome physical contact and sexual overtures, demanding sexual favours, showing pornography against a woman's will, or making sexually coloured remarks, and prescribes varying punishments for these acts.

ingredients.text: A man commits physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures.
A man commits a demand or request for sexual favours.
A man shows pornography against the will of a woman.
A man makes sexually coloured remarks.

354A.punishment: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

354B.heading: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to disrobe.
354B.canonical_text: Any man who assaults or uses criminal force to any woman or abets such act with the intention of disrobing or compelling her to be naked, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

354C.heading: Voyeurism.
354C.canonical_text: This section defines voyeurism as a man watching or capturing the image of a woman engaging in a private act where she expects privacy, or disseminating such an image. It also defines 'private act' and clarifies that dissemination without consent is an offence.

watches, or captures the image of a woman
engaging in a private act
in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by any other person at the behest of the perpetrator
or disseminates such image

“private act” includes an act of watching carried out in a place which, in the circumstances, would reasonably be expected to provide privacy and where the victim's genitals, posterior or breasts are exposed or covered only in underwear; or the victim is using a lavatory; or the victim is doing a sexual act that is not of a kind ordinarily done in public.

Where the victim consents to the capture of the images or any act, but not to their dissemination to third persons and where such image or act is disseminated, such dissemination shall be considered an offence under this section.

On a second or subsequent conviction: imprisonment of either description for a term not less than three years, but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

361.heading: Kidnapping from lawful guardianship.
361.canonical_text: This section defines kidnapping from lawful guardianship as taking or enticing a minor (under 16 for males, under 18 for females) or a person of unsound mind out of the keeping of their lawful guardian without consent. 390.heading: Robbery.
390.canonical_text: Robbery is defined as either theft or extortion committed under specific aggravating circumstances. Theft becomes robbery if the offender, during the act of theft or carrying away property, voluntarily causes or attempts to cause death, hurt, wrongful restraint, or fear of instant death, hurt, or wrongful restraint to any person. Extortion becomes robbery if the offender, while in the presence of the person put in fear, commits the extortion by putting that person or another in fear of instant death, hurt, or wrongful restraint, thereby inducing immediate delivery of the extorted item.

391.heading: Dacoity.

415.heading: Cheating.

The accused made preparation for causing fear of hurt to any person.

punishable with imprisonment for life

450.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

451.heading: House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment.

456.heading: Punishment for lurking house-trespass or house-breaking by night.

Whoever commits house-breaking by night

ingredients.text: The accused made preparation for putting any person in fear of wrongful restraint.

459.heading: Grievous hurt caused whilst committing lurking house-trespass or house-breaking.

ingredients.text: Whoever commits lurking house-trespass or house-breaking

460.canonical_text: If, during lurking house-trespass by night or house-breaking by night, any person involved voluntarily causes or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt, then every person jointly concerned in the offence shall be punished with imprisonment for life or up to ten years, and also be liable to fine.

461.heading: Dishonestly breaking open receptacle containing property.
461.canonical_text: Breaking open or unfastening a closed receptacle containing or believed to contain property, dishonestly or with intent to commit mischief.

ingredients.text: Breaks open or unfastens a closed receptacle.

461.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

462.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

463.heading: Forgery.
463.canonical_text: Whoever makes a false document or electronic record with specific intent, commits forgery.

464.heading: Making a false document.
464.canonical_text: A person is said to make a false document or false electronic record if they dishonestly or fraudulently create, alter, or cause another to create or alter a document or electronic record with the intent to deceive about its origin or authenticity.

ingredients.text: The person makes, signs, seals, executes, makes, or transmits a document or electronic record or part thereof.
The person affixes an electronic signature on an electronic record.
The person makes any mark denoting the execution of a document or the authenticity of an electronic signature.

The person intends to cause it to be believed that such document, electronic record, or electronic signature was made, signed, sealed, executed, transmitted, or affixed by or by the authority of a person.
The person knows that it was not made, signed, sealed, executed, transmitted, or affixed by or by the authority of that person.
The person alters a document or an electronic record in any material part thereof, by cancellation or otherwise.
The alteration occurs after the document or electronic record has been made, executed, or affixed with an electronic signature.
The original document or electronic record was made, executed, or affixed by the person themselves or by any other person, whether living or dead.
The person causes any other person to sign, seal, execute, or alter a document or an electronic record.
The person knows that the other person does not know the contents of the document or electronic record or the nature of the alteration due to deception.

465.heading: Punishment for forgery.

467.heading: Forgery of valuable security, will, etc.
467.canonical_text: Whoever forges a document purporting to be a valuable security, will, authority to adopt a son, or an authority to deal with valuable securities, money, or movable property, or an acquittance/receipt for money or property, shall be punished.

471.canonical_text: This section penalizes the fraudulent or dishonest use of a known or believed forged document or electronic record as genuine, with punishment equivalent to forging the document itself.

The person proves that, on demand made by or on behalf of the prosecutor, they gave all the information in their power with respect to the persons from whom they obtained such goods or things.

486.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

487.heading: Making a false mark upon any receptacle containing goods.
487.canonical_text: This section criminalizes making a false mark on a receptacle containing goods, if done in a manner calculated to deceive about the contents or quality, punishable by imprisonment, fine, or both, unless the accused proves they acted without intent to defraud.

ingredients.text: Whoever makes any false mark upon any case, package or other receptacle containing goods
in a manner reasonably calculated to cause any public servant or any other person to believe
that such receptacle contains goods which it does not contain
or that it does not contain goods which it does contain
or that the goods contained in such receptacle are of a nature or quality different from the real nature or quality thereof
unless he proves that he acted without intent to defraud

487.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both

488.heading: Punishment for making use of any such false mark.
488.canonical_text: This section specifies that whoever uses a false mark in a manner prohibited by the preceding section shall be punished as if they committed an offence against that section, unless they prove they acted without intent to defraud.

ingredients.text: The use is in any manner prohibited by the last foregoing section.

488.punishment: as if he had committed an offence against that section

489.heading: Tampering with property mark with intent to cause injury.
489.canonical_text: This section penalizes anyone who removes, destroys, defaces, or adds to any property mark, intending or knowing it to be likely that such action may cause injury to any person.

ingredients.text: The accused knows it to be likely that he may thereby cause injury to any person

489.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

489A.heading: Counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes.
489A.canonical_text: This section criminalizes counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes, or knowingly participating in the counterfeiting process, and defines 'bank-note' for the purposes of this and related sections.

ingredients.text: Whoever counterfeits
or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting
any currency-note or bank-note

the expression “bank-note” means a promissory note or engagement for the payment of money to bearer on demand issued by any person carrying on the business of banking in any part of the world, or issued by or under the authority of any State or Sovereign Power, and intended to be used as equivalent to, or as a substitute for money

489A.punishment: imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

489B.heading: Using as genuine, forged or counterfeit currency-notes or bank-notes.
489B.canonical_text: Whoever sells, buys, receives, traffics in, or uses as genuine, any forged or counterfeit currency-note or bank-note, knowing or having reason to believe it is forged or counterfeit, shall be punished.

ingredients.text: The accused sells to another person a currency-note or bank-note.
The accused buys or receives from another person a currency-note or bank-note.
The accused traffics in a currency-note or bank-note.
The accused uses as genuine a currency-note or bank-note.
The currency-note or bank-note is forged or counterfeit.

489B.punishment: imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

489C.heading: Possession of forged or counterfeit currency notes or bank-notes.
489C.canonical_text: This section penalizes the possession of forged or counterfeit currency notes or bank-notes with the intent to use them as genuine, knowing or having reason to believe they are forged or counterfeit.

ingredients.text: The accused intends to use the currency-note or bank-note as genuine or intends that it may be used as genuine

489C.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

489D.heading: Making or possessing instruments or materials for forging or counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes.
489D.canonical_text: This section prohibits making, possessing, buying, selling, or disposing of any machinery, instrument, or material intended for forging or counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes, with penalties including life imprisonment or up to ten years, plus a fine.

ingredients.text: Whoever makes, or performs any part of the process of making, or buys or sells or disposes of, or has in his possession

normalized.action: makes OR performs part of process OR buys OR sells OR disposes of OR possesses

ingredients.text: any machinery, instrument or material
for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used

normalized.intent: purpose of use OR knowledge/reason to believe intended use

ingredients.text: for forging or counterfeiting any currency-note or bank-note

489D.punishment: imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

489E.heading: Making or using documents resembling currency-notes or bank-notes.
489E.canonical_text: This section prohibits making, using, or delivering documents that resemble currency or bank notes with intent to deceive, and penalizes individuals whose names appear on such documents for refusing to disclose the maker's details to a police officer. It also establishes a presumption regarding the maker of the document.

ingredients.text: Whoever makes, or causes to be made, or uses for any purpose whatsoever, or delivers to any person, any document.
The document purports to be, or in any way resembles, or so nearly resembles as to be calculated to deceive, any currency-note or bank-note.
If any person, whose name appears on a document the making of which is an offence under sub-section (1).
That person refuses, without lawful excuse, to disclose to a police-officer on being so required the name and address of the person by whom it was printed or otherwise made.

489E.punishment: fine which may extend to two hundred rupees

490.heading: [Repealed.].
490.canonical_text: This section, which dealt with breach of contract of service during voyage or journey, has been repealed.

status.note: Repealed by the Workmen's Breach of Contract (Repealing) Act, 1925 (3 of 1925), s. 2 and Sch.

491.heading: Breach of contract to attend on and supply wants of helpless person.
491.canonical_text: This section punishes anyone who, being legally bound by contract to care for a helpless person, voluntarily fails to do so, with imprisonment, fine, or both.

ingredients.text: Whoever, being bound by a lawful contract to attend on or to supply the wants of any person
who, by reason of youth, or of unsoundness of mind, or of a disease or bodily weakness, is helpless or incapable of providing for his own safety or of supplying his own wants
voluntarily omits so to do

491.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both.

492.heading: [Repealed.].
492.canonical_text: This section, which dealt with breach of contract to serve at a distant place where the servant was conveyed at the master's expense, has been repealed by the Workmen's Breach of Contract (Repealing) Act, 1925.

ingredients.text: Breach of contract to serve at distant place to which servant is conveyed at master's expense.

status.note: Rep. by the Workmen's Breach of Contract (Repealing) Act, 1925 (3 of 1925), s. 2 and Sch.

493.heading: Cohabitation caused by a man deceitfully inducing a belief of lawful marriage.
493.canonical_text: A man by deceit causes a woman, not lawfully married to him, to believe she is lawfully married and to cohabit or have sexual intercourse with him based on that belief.

ingredients.text: Every man
by deceit causes
any woman who is not lawfully married to him
to believe that she is lawfully married to him
and to cohabit or have sexual intercourse with him in that belief

493.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

494.heading: Marrying again during life-time of husband or wife.
494.canonical_text: This section criminalizes marrying again while a previous husband or wife is still living, rendering the subsequent marriage void, and provides specific exceptions to this offense.

ingredients.text: A person has a husband or wife living.
The subsequent marriage is void by reason of its taking place during the life of the first husband or wife.
The previous marriage with such husband or wife has been declared void by a Court of competent jurisdiction.
The former husband or wife has been continually absent from such person for the space of seven years at the time of the subsequent marriage.
The former husband or wife has not been heard of by such person as being alive within that seven-year period.

The person contracting such subsequent marriage informs the person with whom such marriage is contracted of the real state of facts before such marriage takes place, so far as the same are within his or her knowledge.

494.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

495.heading: Same offence with concealment of former marriage from person with whom subsequent marriage is contracted.
495.canonical_text: Whoever commits the offence of bigamy, having concealed the fact of the former marriage from the person with whom the subsequent marriage is contracted, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and fine.

ingredients.text: Whoever commits the offence defined in the last preceding section
having concealed from the person with whom the subsequent marriage is contracted, the fact of the former marriage

495.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

496.heading: Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage.
496.canonical_text: Whoever, dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention, goes through a marriage ceremony, knowing it is not a lawful marriage.

ingredients.text: Whoever, dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention, goes through the ceremony of being married
knowing that he is not thereby lawfully married

496.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

497.heading: Adultery.
497.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of adultery as sexual intercourse by a man with another man's wife, without the husband's consent or connivance, and not amounting to rape, where the perpetrator knows or has reason to believe she is married. It prescribes punishment and clarifies that the wife is not punishable as an abettor.

ingredients.text: Whoever has sexual intercourse with a person
who is the wife of another man
whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the wife of another man
without the consent of that man
without the connivance of that man
such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape

497.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both

498.heading: Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman.
498.canonical_text: This section criminalizes taking, enticing, concealing, or detaining a married woman, whom the accused knows or believes to be married, from her husband or guardian, with the intent for her to engage in illicit intercourse. The punishment includes imprisonment up to two years, a fine, or both.

ingredients.text: The accused takes or entices away a woman.
The accused conceals or detains a woman.
The woman is the wife of another man.
The accused knows or has reason to believe the woman is the wife of another man.

498.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

498A.heading: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.
498A.canonical_text: This section defines cruelty against a woman by her husband or his relatives and prescribes punishment for such acts.

ingredients.text: The accused subjects such woman to cruelty.
The cruelty is any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide.
The cruelty is any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman.

normalized.effect: grave injury or danger to life, limb or health

ingredients.text: The cruelty is harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security.
The cruelty is harassment of the woman where such harassment is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such unlawful demand for any property or valuable security.

498A.punishment: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine

499.heading: Defamation.
499.canonical_text: Defamation occurs when a person makes or publishes an imputation by words, signs, or visible representations, intending or knowing it will harm another's reputation, unless an exception applies. This includes imputations against deceased persons, companies, or made ironically, and harm to reputation is specifically defined.

ingredients.text: Whoever makes or publishes any imputation.
The imputation is made by words (spoken or intended to be read), or by signs, or by visible representations.

Harm to a person's reputation occurs if the imputation directly or indirectly, in the estimation of others, lowers the moral or intellectual character of that person, or lowers the character of that person in respect of his caste or of his calling, or lowers the credit of that person, or causes it to be believed that the body of that person is in a loathsome state, or in a state generally considered as disgraceful.
An imputation to a deceased person may amount to defamation if it would harm their reputation if living, and is intended to be hurtful to the feelings of their family or other near relatives.
An imputation concerning a company or an association or collection of persons as such may amount to defamation.
An imputation in the form of an alternative or expressed ironically may amount to defamation.

500.heading: Punishment for defamation.
500.canonical_text: Defamation is punishable by simple imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
500.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

501.heading: Printing or engraving matter known to be defamatory.
501.canonical_text: This section penalizes printing or engraving defamatory matter with knowledge or belief of its defamatory nature.

ingredients.text: Whoever prints or engraves any matter
knowing or having good reason to believe

normalized.mental_state: knowing or having good reason to believe

ingredients.text: that such matter is defamatory of any person

501.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

502.heading: Sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter.
502.canonical_text: This section penalizes the sale or offer for sale of printed or engraved material containing defamatory matter, when done with knowledge of its defamatory content.

ingredients.text: Whoever sells or offers for sale
any printed or engraved substance
containing defamatory matter
knowing that it contains such matter

502.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

503.heading: Criminal intimidation.
503.canonical_text: Criminal intimidation is committed when a person threatens another with injury to their person, reputation, or property, or to someone they are interested in, with the intent to cause alarm, or to compel them to act or omit an act they are not legally bound to do or are legally entitled to do, as a means to avoid the threat's execution.

ingredients.text: The intent is to cause alarm to the threatened person.
A threat to injure the reputation of any deceased person in whom the threatened person is interested falls within the scope of this section.

504.heading: Intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace.
504.canonical_text: Whoever intentionally insults a person, thereby giving provocation, with the intent or knowledge that such provocation is likely to cause a breach of public peace or the commission of another offence.

ingredients.text: The insult gives provocation to that person.
The accused intends or knows it to be likely that such provocation will cause the person to break the public peace.
The accused intends or knows it to be likely that such provocation will cause the person to commit any other offence.

504.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

505.heading: Statements conducing to public mischief.
505.canonical_text: This section criminalizes making, publishing, or circulating any statement, rumour, or report with the intent or likelihood to cause mutiny or dereliction of duty in the armed forces, create public fear or alarm leading to offenses against the State or public tranquility, or incite enmity between different classes or communities. It also specifically addresses creating or promoting enmity on grounds such as religion, race, or caste, with an aggravated punishment if committed in a place of worship. An exception applies if the statement is believed to be true and circulated in good faith without malicious intent.

ingredients.text: Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement, rumour or report
with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such

with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against the public tranquility
with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit any offence against any other class or community

Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing rumour or alarming news with intent to create or promote, or which is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill- will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities
commits an offence specified in sub-section (2) in any place of worship or in any assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies

It does not amount to an offence when the person making, publishing or circulating any such statement, rumour or report, has reasonable grounds for believing that such statement, rumour or report is true and makes, publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid

505.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both (up to five years and fine for offenses in places of worship).

506.heading: Punishment for criminal intimidation.
506.canonical_text: This section prescribes the punishment for criminal intimidation, detailing a general punishment and an enhanced punishment for specific types of threats, including those causing death, grievous hurt, property destruction by fire, serious offences, or imputing unchastity to a woman.

ingredients.text: Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation
if the threat be to cause death or grievous hurt
or to cause the destruction of any property by fire
or to cause an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years
or to impute unchastity to a woman

506.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; or, for aggravated threats, imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

507.heading: Criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication.
507.canonical_text: This section prescribes enhanced punishment for criminal intimidation committed through anonymous communication or by concealing the identity of the threatener.

ingredients.text: Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication
or having taken precaution to conceal the name or abode of the person from whom the threat comes

507.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, in addition to the punishment provided for the offence by the last preceding section.

508.heading: Act caused by inducing person to believe that he will be rendered an object of the Divine displeasure.
508.canonical_text: This section defines the offence of voluntarily causing or attempting to cause a person to act or omit by inducing a belief that they or someone they are interested in will become an object of Divine displeasure due to the offender's act, if they do not comply with the offender's objective.

ingredients.text: The offender voluntarily causes or attempts to cause any person to do something which that person is not legally bound to do, or to omit something which that person is legally entitled to do.
The offender induces or attempts to induce that person to believe that they or any person in whom they are interested will become an object of Divine displeasure.

508.punishment: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

509.heading: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman.
509.canonical_text: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any words, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman.

ingredients.text: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman,

normalized.intent: to insult the modesty of any woman

ingredients.text: utters any words,
makes any sound or gesture,
or exhibits any object,
intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman,

normalized.intent: word/sound heard by woman OR gesture/object seen by woman

ingredients.text: or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman,

normalized.action: intrudes upon the privacy of such woman

509.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine

510.heading: Misconduct in public by a drunken person.
510.canonical_text: A person who, while intoxicated, appears in a public place or a place they trespass, and causes annoyance, is subject to simple imprisonment or fine or both.

ingredients.text: Whoever, in a state of intoxication
appears in any public place
or in any place which it is a trespass in him to enter
and there conducts himself in such a manner as to cause annoyance to any person

510.punishment: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to twenty-four hours, or with fine which may extend to ten rupees, or with both

511.heading: Punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment.
511.canonical_text: This section prescribes punishment for attempting to commit an offence punishable by this Code with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment, or causing such an offence to be committed, where an act is done towards its commission and no express provision for such attempt's punishment exists elsewhere in the Code.

ingredients.text: Whoever attempts to commit an offence
The offence is punishable by this Code with imprisonment for life or imprisonment
or attempts to cause such an offence to be committed
and in such attempt does any act towards the commission of the offence
where no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such attempt

511.punishment: Imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the imprisonment for life or, as the case may be, one- half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence, or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both.
